### Real Estate SEO - Win Listings and Buyers from Google
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/real-estate-seo
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-07-06
- **Description:** SEO for real estate agencies: rank for area searches, attract sellers who want an agent, and turn Google traffic into listings and buyer enquiries.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: I already post to property portals - what does SEO add?
    A: Portals rent you an audience. Your site captures one you own. Listings and seller leads that come through your pages avoid per-listing fees and side-by-side competitor clutter.
  - Q: How fast will real estate SEO show results?
    A: Seller searches in specific areas often have lower competition - top rankings in 2–4 months are realistic. Area guides and valuation content compound for years.
  - Q: Do real estate agencies need a new website for SEO?
    A: If the current site cannot support area pages and fast mobile listing search, yes. Structure and speed decide whether enquiries convert.
  - Q: How much does real estate SEO cost?
    A: Agencies targeting two or three areas often fit Foundations at €500/mo. Multi-area, international, or portal-style sites usually need Growth at €900/mo or higher.
  - Q: Should agencies target buyers or sellers first?
    A: Both, but sellers are usually higher value. “How much is my home worth” and “estate agent + area” pages win listings - the root of agency income.

### SEO for Beginners - A 30-Day Plan
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/seo-for-beginners
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-07-06
- **Description:** SEO for beginners: how Google ranks pages, the four pillars, a 30-day starter plan, glossary links, and the fixes to make before you publish more.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: What is SEO for beginners?
    A: SEO for beginners is the work of helping a website show up in unpaid Google results. You start with crawling, indexing, one clear page per customer question, and measurement in Search Console. It is the same discipline as professional SEO, with a smaller first scope.
  - Q: How do I start SEO as a beginner?
    A: Verify the site in Google Search Console, fix anything that blocks indexing, and give each important page one primary query plus a clear title. Follow a 30-day plan before you publish a large blog archive.
  - Q: Can I do SEO myself?
    A: Yes for the basics - titles, a complete Google Business Profile, and pages that answer real customer questions. Technical repairs, strategy, and earning links are where a specialist usually saves time.
  - Q: How long does SEO take for beginners?
    A: Plan for early signs in 2–3 months and a clearer picture in 4–6 months if the technical base is fixed and the important pages are improved on a steady cadence. A new site should not expect a full pipeline in the first weeks.
  - Q: Should a beginner use SEO or Google Ads?
    A: They do different jobs. Ads can bring visits while you pay for each click. SEO builds organic visibility that remains when ad spend pauses. Many businesses use both, and the landing pages should be ready before you scale ads.
  - Q: What should a beginner measure first?
    A: Impressions and clicks in Search Console, whether the money pages are indexed, and whether organic visits turn into calls or form fills. A rank position by itself does not show that the channel is working.

### SEO ή Google Ads; Τι Συμφέρει το 2026
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/el/blog/seo-i-google-ads
- **Locale:** el · **Date:** 2026-07-06
- **Description:** SEO ή Google Ads: κόστος, χρόνος και απόδοση σε σύγκριση, με παραδείγματα από ελληνικές επιχειρήσεις και πότε αξίζει να τρέχουν μαζί.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: Μπορώ να κάνω μόνο Google Ads;
    A: Μπορείτε, αλλά νοικιάζετε κίνηση για πάντα. Επιπλέον, μια αργή ιστοσελίδα με κακές σελίδες πληρώνει ακριβότερα και τα Ads (χαμηλό Quality Score = υψηλότερο CPC).
  - Q: Το SEO δουλεύει για μικρές επιχειρήσεις;
    A: Ειδικά για αυτές. Στις τοπικές αναζητήσεις ο ανταγωνισμός είναι μικρότερος και μια καλή στρατηγική τοπικού SEO φέρνει κυριαρχία στην περιοχή με λογικό κόστος έναντι αυξανόμενων CPC.
  - Q: Ποια κατανομή budget προτείνετε;
    A: Οι περισσότερες ΜμΕ τα πάνε καλά με Ads για άμεση ζήτηση τους μήνες 1–3 παράλληλα με θεμέλια SEO, και σταδιακή μετάβαση προς περίπου 70% SEO / 30% Ads καθώς ανεβαίνει η οργανική κίνηση.
  - Q: Πότε το SEO γίνεται φθηνότερο ανά lead από τα Ads;
    A: Συχνά στους μήνες 4–8 για τοπικές ή μεσαίας δυσκολίας λέξεις, αν διορθώσετε τεχνικά και βελτιώσετε σελίδες υπηρεσιών. Εθνικοί όροι υψηλού ανταγωνισμού χρειάζονται περισσότερο χρόνο.
  - Q: Ποιος πρέπει να τρέχει και τα δύο;
    A: Η στρατηγική αποδίδει όταν Ads και SEO μοιράζονται δεδομένα λέξεων-κλειδιών και landing pages. Ένας συνεργάτης (ή στενά συντονισμένες ομάδες) αποφεύγει αντικρουόμενες προσφορές και σπατάλη.

### SEO vs Google Ads - Which Is Right for Your Business in 2026?
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/seo-vs-google-ads
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-07-06
- **Description:** SEO or Google Ads? A clear comparison of cost, speed, ROI, common mistakes and when the 70/30 mix wins, so your budget goes where it actually pays.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: Can I run only Ads and skip SEO?
    A: You can, but you rent traffic forever. A slow site with poor pages also pays more for Ads (low Quality Score = higher CPC). Fix landing pages either way.
  - Q: Does SEO work for small businesses?
    A: Especially for them. Local searches are less competitive, and a good local SEO strategy delivers area dominance at a sensible cost compared with rising CPCs.
  - Q: What budget split should I use?
    A: Most SMEs do well with Ads for immediate demand in months 1–3 while SEO foundations run in parallel, then gradually shift toward a 70% SEO / 30% Ads mix as organic traffic grows.
  - Q: How long until SEO beats Ads on cost per lead?
    A: Often by months 4–8 for local or mid-competition niches if you fix technical basics and optimize service pages. Competitive national terms take longer.
  - Q: Who should run both channels?
    A: The strategy pays off when Ads and SEO share keyword and landing-page data. One partner (or tightly aligned teams) prevents conflicting offers and wasted spend.

### Web Hosting & Domain - A 2026 Buyer's Guide
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/web-hosting-domain-guide
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-07-06
- **Description:** How to choose hosting and a domain for your website: pricing, speed, security, and the mistakes that quietly cost you SEO rankings and credibility.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: What's the total cost of ownership of a website?
    A: Domain about €12/year, hosting €120–€400/year, plus optional maintenance from €199/month. The full picture depends on site type - see our website cost guide.
  - Q: Can I change hosting without losing SEO?
    A: Yes. Moving hosting does not change URLs, so rankings stay intact if you avoid downtime and handle DNS correctly. A redesign is different and needs a migration plan.
  - Q: Does my e-shop need different hosting?
    A: Yes: more RAM (at least 2–4 GB), object caching (Redis), enough PHP workers, and more frequent backups. Cheap €3–€5 shared plans rarely survive busy WooCommerce traffic.
  - Q: Should I register a country TLD or .com?
    A: Use a country TLD for a single local market. Use .com for international targeting (tourism, exports, SaaS). If you serve both, register both and set one as primary with redirects.
  - Q: Should business email live on the same hosting plan?
    A: No. Prefer Google Workspace or Microsoft 365. Hosting email often lands in spam and complicates DNS/SPF when you migrate the site.

### Web Hosting & Domain στην Ελλάδα - Οδηγός Επιλογής 2026
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/el/blog/web-hosting-domain-odigos
- **Locale:** el · **Date:** 2026-07-06
- **Description:** Πώς να επιλέξετε hosting και domain για την ιστοσελίδα σας. Τιμές, .gr ή .com, ταχύτητα, ασφάλεια και τα λάθη που κοστίζουν σε SEO και αξιοπιστία.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: Πόσο κοστίζει συνολικά η συντήρηση ζωής μιας ιστοσελίδας;
    A: Domain περίπου €12/χρόνο, hosting €120–€400/χρόνο και προαιρετική τεχνική συντήρηση από €199/μήνα. Το συνολικό κόστος εξαρτάται από τον τύπο site - δείτε και τον οδηγό πόσο κοστίζει μια ιστοσελίδα.
  - Q: Μπορώ να αλλάξω hosting χωρίς να χάσω το SEO;
    A: Ναι. Η μεταφορά hosting δεν αλλάζει URLs, άρα δεν αγγίζει κατατάξεις, αρκεί να γίνει χωρίς downtime και με σωστό DNS χειρισμό. Διαφορετικό θέμα είναι ο ανασχεδιασμός, που θέλει migration πλάνο.
  - Q: Το e-shop μου θέλει διαφορετικό hosting;
    A: Ναι: περισσότερη μνήμη (τουλάχιστον 2–4 GB RAM), object caching (Redis/Object Cache Pro), PHP workers και συχνότερα backups. Shared πακέτα €3–€5 σπάνια αντέχουν WooCommerce με κίνηση.
  - Q: .gr ή .com - τι να κατοχυρώσω;
    A: Για ελληνική αγορά προτιμήστε .gr. Για διεθνή στόχευση (τουρισμός, εξαγωγές) προτιμήστε .com. Αν απευθύνεστε και στα δύο κοινά, κατοχυρώστε και τα δύο και ορίστε το ένα ως κύριο με σωστά redirects.
  - Q: Πρέπει το εταιρικό email να είναι στο ίδιο hosting με το site;
    A: Όχι. Προτιμήστε Google Workspace ή Microsoft 365. Το hosting email καταλήγει συχνά στα spam και μπερδεύει DNS/SPF όταν μεταφέρετε το site.

### Website Redesign Without Losing Your SEO
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/website-redesign-guide
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-07-06
- **Description:** When to redesign a website, what it costs, and how to do it with a safe SEO migration so you don't lose rankings and organic traffic.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: Will I lose rankings during a redesign?
    A: With a proper migration, the dip is usually limited to a few positions for 1–2 weeks and is often followed by a rise because the new site is faster and better structured.
  - Q: How much does a website redesign cost?
    A: Typically €1,500–€4,000 depending on size, because it includes carrying over SEO history. Cheap redesigns that skip migration cost far more in lost traffic.
  - Q: Can I keep the same domain?
    A: Yes - and you should. The domain carries your credibility. Changing domain and redesigning at once is double risk and needs special handling.
  - Q: Redesign or a brand-new site?
    A: If the site has organic traffic, redesign with migration. If it is invisible in Google and technically broken, a new build is often cleaner.
  - Q: How long does a safe redesign take?
    A: Typically 3–6 weeks after inventory and redirect mapping, depending on page count, languages, and booking/e-commerce complexity.

### Σχεδιασμός Ιστοσελίδας Τουρισμού 2026 - Τάσεις, SEO και UX
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/el/blog/sxediasmos-istoselidas-tourismos-2026

- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: Τι είναι προτιμότερο: μινιμαλιστικό ή πλούσιο σε περιεχόμενο design;
    A: Το πλούσιο σε περιεχόμενο design κερδίζει στο SEO και το AEO. Διατηρήστε καθαρή αισθητική με accordions και ξεκάθαρη ιεραρχία - το κείμενο πρέπει να είναι προσβάσιμο στα bots.
  - Q: Πόσο συχνά πρέπει να γίνεται ανασχεδιασμός;
    A: Ριζικός ανασχεδιασμός κάθε 3–4 χρόνια. Περιεχόμενο, FAQs και έλεγχοι ταχύτητας ανά τρίμηνο. Αν έχετε κατατάξεις, προτιμήστε migration - δείτε τον οδηγό ανασχεδιασμού.

  - Q: Χρειάζομαι chatbot AI στην ιστοσελίδα τουρισμού;
    A: Όχι υποχρεωτικά την πρώτη μέρα, αλλά βοηθά σε άμεσες απαντήσεις εκτός ωραρίου. Συνδυάστε το με καθαρά FAQs και booking CTA - δείτε τον οδηγό AI chatbots στον τουρισμό.
  - Q: Ποιες γλώσσες χρειάζομαι;
    A: Ελληνικά και Αγγλικά είναι η βάση. Γερμανικά/Γαλλικά αξίζουν όταν στοχεύετε αγορές υψηλής αξίας - πάντα με σωστό hreflang.

### Τοπικό SEO στις Κυκλάδες - Οδηγός για Ξενοδοχεία και Rent-a-Car
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/el/blog/topiko-seo-kykladon
- **Locale:** el · **Date:** 2026-06-18

- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: Ποιο νησί είναι πιο εύκολο για τοπικό SEO στις Κυκλάδες;
    A: Νησιά με χαμηλότερο ανταγωνισμό (Μήλος, Τήνος, Φολέγανδρος, Κύθνος) δίνουν πιο γρήγορα αποτελέσματα από Μύκονο και Σαντορίνη. Η στρατηγική προσαρμόζεται στη δυσκολία της αγοράς.
  - Q: Χρειάζομαι ξεχωριστό Google Business Profile για κάθε νησί;
    A: Ναι, εφόσον διατηρείτε φυσικό γραφείο ή σημείο εξυπηρέτησης στο συγκεκριμένο νησί. Αυτό αυξάνει κατακόρυφα την εμφάνιση στους τοπικούς χάρτες.

    A: Με σωστό GBP, citations και location pages, τα πρώτα αποτελέσματα εμφανίζονται σε 8–12 εβδομάδες. Σε πολύ ανταγωνιστικά νησιά η διαδικασία μπορεί να διαρκέσει 4–6 μήνες.
  - Q: Πρέπει το SEO να είναι πολύγλωσσο στις Κυκλάδες;
    A: Ναι, για τα περισσότερα τουριστικά brands. Ελληνικά και Αγγλικά είναι βάση· Γερμανικά/Γαλλικά όπου η ζήτηση το δικαιολογεί, πάντα με σωστό hreflang.
  - Q: Πόσο κοστίζει το τοπικό SEO για ξενοδοχείο ή rent-a-car στις Κυκλάδες;
    A: Τυπικά €500–€900/μήνα για ένα νησί· €900–€1.500+/μήνα για ανταγωνιστικούς προορισμούς ή πολλά σημεία. Δείτε τα πακέτα τιμολόγησης.

### Τι Πρέπει να Έχει η Ιστοσελίδα Ξενοδοχείου
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/el/blog/kataskevi-istoselidas-xenodoxeia
- **Locale:** el · **Date:** 2026-06-17
- **Description:** Τι πρέπει να έχει μια ιστοσελίδα ξενοδοχείου το 2026: σελίδες δωματίων, booking engine, ταχύτητα, SEO και schema για περισσότερες άμεσες κρατήσεις.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: Πόσο κοστίζει ιστοσελίδα ξενοδοχείου;
    A: Τυπικά €1.500–€3.500 για site με κρατήσεις. Στα πακέτα μας, Professional (€2.500) ή Business (€4.000) καλύπτουν τις περισσότερες μονάδες, με SEO θεμέλια από την 1η μέρα.
  - Q: Γιατί να επενδύσω σε direct bookings;
    A: Κάθε κράτηση μέσω Booking/Expedia κοστίζει 15–25% προμήθεια. Άμεσες κρατήσεις από το δικό σας site μειώνουν το κόστος και σας δίνουν τον πελάτη.
  - Q: Χρειάζομαι booking engine;
    A: Ναι, αν θέλετε πραγματικές απευθείας κρατήσεις. Εναλλακτικά, φόρμα διαθεσιμότητας + WhatsApp μπορεί να αρκεί για μικρές μονάδες - το σχεδιάζουμε μαζί σας.
  - Q: Μπορεί η ιστοσελίδα μου να ανταγωνιστεί το Booking.com στο SEO;
    A: Στις γενικές αναζητήσεις είναι δύσκολο, αλλά σε brand και long-tail (π.χ. luxury suites με ιδιωτική πισίνα) η δική σας ιστοσελίδα μπορεί να κατακτήσει την πρώτη θέση.
  - Q: Πόσο διαρκεί η κατασκευή ιστοσελίδας ξενοδοχείου;
    A: Συνήθως 3–5 εβδομάδες μόλις είναι έτοιμες φωτογραφίες, περιγραφές δωματίων και πολιτικές. Το περιεχόμενο είναι ο συνηθέστερος λόγος καθυστέρησης.

    A: Σε πολύ ανταγωνιστικούς προορισμούς 6–12 μήνες. Σε νησιά με μικρότερο ανταγωνισμό, συχνά 8–16 εβδομάδες με συστηματική δουλειά.

    A: Και τα δύο, αλλά οι location pages (αεροδρόμιο/λιμάνι) συχνά φέρνουν τις υψηλότερης πρόθεσης κρατήσεις. Ο στόλος κλείνει τη σύγκριση τιμής/τύπου.

### AI Chatbots στον Τουρισμό - 24/7 Κρατήσεις και AEO
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/el/blog/ai-chatbots-tourismos
- **Locale:** el · **Date:** 2026-06-15
- **Description:** Πώς τα έξυπνα AI Chatbots μεταμορφώνουν την εξυπηρέτηση πελατών στον τουρισμό. Αυτοματοποίηση κρατήσεων, απαντήσεις σε FAQ και GEO/AEO ορατότητα.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: Μπορεί το AI Chatbot να κάνει λάθη στις απαντήσεις του;
    A: Με guardrails και RAG πάνω στη δική σας knowledge base, το bot απαντά μόνο από τιμές, πολιτικές και παροχές σας. Χωρίς αυτά, τα γενικά LLM επινοούν - γι’ αυτό δεν αρκεί «ένα ChatGPT widget».
  - Q: Πώς συνδέεται το Chatbot με τις κρατήσεις;
    A: Καθοδηγεί τον χρήστη σε διαθέσιμα δωμάτια/οχήματα και δίνει deep link στη σελίδα ολοκλήρωσης κράτησης - δεν αντικαθιστά απαραίτητα το booking engine.
  - Q: Βοηθάει το chatbot το SEO και το AEO;
    A: Ναι, όταν οι συχνές ερωτήσεις του chat γίνονται FAQ στη σελίδα με schema. Έτσι κερδίζετε snippets/Overviews και τροφοδοτείτε GEO citations από τις ίδιες κανονικές απαντήσεις.
  - Q: Επιβαρύνει την ταχύτητα της ιστοσελίδας;
    A: Μόνο αν φορτώνει blocking. Το widget πρέπει να φορτώνει ασύγχρονα μετά το LCP. Ένα κακό chatbot που σκοτώνει Core Web Vitals βλάπτει SEO και μετατροπές.
  - Q: Χρειάζομαι chatbot ή πρώτα Ορατότητα σε AI;
    A: Συχνά και τα δύο - το chatbot εξυπηρετεί επισκέπτες· η υπηρεσία GEO/AEO κάνει τις σελίδες σας citable σε ChatGPT/Perplexity. Ξεκινήστε από καθαρή knowledge base κοινής χρήσης.

### GEO, AEO & AI SEO - Global Playbook for 2026
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/geo-aeo-global-seo-playbook
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-05-31
- **Description:** Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and traditional SEO: how teams rank on Google, ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: Is GEO replacing SEO?
    A: No. Most commercial traffic still comes from Google blue links and map packs. GEO is additive - a visibility layer for AI-mediated discovery. Neglect SEO and you lose the foundation.
  - Q: What's the fastest AEO win?
    A: Add FAQ sections with schema to your top 10 GSC pages by impressions. Match questions to real queries. Keep answers concise and visible on-page.
  - Q: Can small tourism businesses compete in AI answers?
    A: Yes. Models often cite specific, authoritative local sources over generic OTAs when the content is clearer and more recent.
  - Q: How do I measure GEO success?
    A: Track citation rate across a fixed prompt set, citation accuracy, and competitor coverage gaps. Pair with branded organic click trends.
  - Q: Do I need separate content for ChatGPT vs Google?
    A: No. Write clear, factual, well-structured content for humans. Both classic search and generative systems reward clarity, authority, and freshness.

### SEO Software, Web Design & Development Platform
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/seo-web-design-development-platform
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-05-31
- **Description:** How teams combine SEO tools, website design for rankings, and development best practices with AI search optimization (GEO/AEO) to grow revenue.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: Should SEO come before or after design?
    A: At the same time. SEO informs information architecture, URL planning, and template requirements before high-fidelity design. Bolting SEO on after development costs more and works worse.
  - Q: Do I need custom development or is WordPress enough?
    A: Both can rank. Custom Next.js stacks offer performance and component consistency at scale - valuable for multi-property hospitality and rent-a-car fleets. WordPress works for smaller footprints with strict maintenance discipline.
  - Q: How do Core Web Vitals affect AI visibility?
    A: Indirectly but meaningfully. Slow, poorly indexed pages are less likely to be retrieved and cited. Performance is a baseline eligibility factor, not a vanity metric.
  - Q: Can one agency handle design, dev, and SEO?
    A: Yes - if they show integrated case studies with Search Console outcomes, not only design shots. Ask for work samples with measurable search results.
  - Q: What's the first step for a redesign without losing rankings?
    A: Crawl the current site, map URL redirects, export top GSC pages, and lock the redirect + content migration plan before touching the new design system.

### Why we split software pricing and agency pricing (and how to choose)
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/pricing-page-seo-software-vs-agency
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-03-10
- **Description:** Clear positioning between self-serve SEO software and done-for-you retainers on your pricing page, which reduces confusion and improves lead quality.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: Is software cheaper than agency?
    A: Lower cash cost - higher time cost. Total cost of ownership includes your hours or opportunity cost.
  - Q: Can I switch from software to agency mid-year?
    A: Yes - export GSC history and backlog. Good agencies start from data.
  - Q: Do you need agency for [GEO/AEO](/el/blog/geo-vs-seo-vs-aeo-el)?
    A: FAQ and entity content can be agency or in-house. LLM measurement discipline benefits from experienced guidance initially.
  - Q: Should startups buy agency day one?
    A: If website doesn't exist or doesn't rank - agency project often beats software alone. If learning phase - software + DIY path.
  - Q: How do I compare agency quotes?
    A: Same scope definition: pages delivered, GBP locations, reporting cadence, redesign inclusion. Apples-to-apples.

### A one-hour Google Search Console ops loop for in-house teams
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/gsc-weekly-ops-playbook
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-03-08
- **Description:** A repeatable weekly Search Console checklist: segment performance, cluster queries, pick three items to ship and validate the results in rank tracking.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: What if I miss a week?
    A: Don't double the workload - resume with one week export and three fixes. Consistency beats catch-up marathons.
  - Q: Is one hour enough for large sites?
    A: For enterprise, scale clustering with tools - but keep three-fix ship cap per property or cluster. Multi-property hotel groups run loop per brand or region.
  - Q: Should I include Bing Webmaster Tools?
    A: Optional monthly - Google priority for most tourism and local markets.
  - Q: How do I involve developers?
    A: Ticket only technical fixes with repro steps and expected measurable outcome - indexation count, LCP on template, structured data validation.
  - Q: When do I need an agency instead?
    A: If three fixes/week backlog exceeds 8 weeks consistently - get scoped help.

### Using an SEO glossary to strengthen internal links (without spam)
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/glossary-strategy-internal-linking
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-03-05
- **Description:** How glossary hubs support entity clarity, hub-and-spoke linking and safer anchor patterns, with a workflow that points readers to product modules.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: How many glossary terms do I need?
    A: Start with 20–30 tied to your top queries and sales conversations. Expand as content gaps appear - don't publish 500 thin definitions day one.
  - Q: Should glossary pages index?
    A: Yes - if they provide unique definitions. No - if they're thin duplicates of blog content. Merge or differentiate.
  - Q: Can glossary replace FAQ?
    A: No - FAQ answers customer-specific questions on commercial pages. Glossary defines concepts. Use both.
  - Q: Multilingual glossaries?
    A: For EL/EN tourism sites, mirror key terms with hreflang. See GEO/AEO Ellada.
  - Q: Who writes glossary entries?
    A: SEO lead outlines entities; subject expert validates accuracy; developer implements linking templates. For hotel and rent-a-car sites, involve front-desk or fleet managers who field guest questions daily.

### Internal Linking Audit Checklist for In-House SEO Teams
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/internal-linking-audit-checklist
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-02-18
- **Description:** Find orphan pages, over-linked footers and anchor text patterns that waste crawl budget, with a pragmatic fix order for tourism and local business sites.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: How many internal links per page?
    A: No fixed limit - prioritize relevance. Long guides may have 10–20 contextual links; short pages need fewer. Avoid footer spam.
  - Q: Should I link to external sites?
    A: Yes - authoritative outbound links support E-E-A-T. Link to tourism boards, official airport sites, medical sources as appropriate.
  - Q: Do internal links pass PageRank?
    A: Google uses links to understand importance and discovery. Internal links distribute signals within your site - link equity concepts still apply internally.
  - Q: Can I automate internal linking?
    A: Plugins and rules help at scale - but review for relevance. Automated "related posts" often link irrelevant URLs.
  - Q: How do I measure impact?
    A: Compare GSC clicks on target URLs 4–8 weeks post-fix. Track orphan count monthly.

### LLM Citations and Brand Visibility - A Sober Measurement Guide
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/llm-citations-brand-visibility
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-02-14
- **Description:** What “being cited by AI” means for your brand, how to sample AI answers responsibly, and how to connect citation work to real business outcomes.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: How is LLM visibility different from featured snippets?
    A: Featured snippets are Google's direct answers with known SERP tracking. LLM citations happen across multiple models with less transparency. Optimize for both with FAQ-rich, factual content.
  - Q: Should I pay for "AI SEO" tools?
    A: Evaluate tools on workflow value - prompt batching, logging, trend charts - not magic scores. Ground decisions in Search Console and bookings.
  - Q: Do AI models use my site in real time?
    A: Some products retrieve live web results; others rely on training data and retrieval indexes. Behavior varies by model and query - log version and date every sample.
  - Q: Can negative AI mentions hurt my brand?
    A: Inaccurate paraphrases happen. Monitor accuracy, publish corrections on-site, and strengthen entity signals. You cannot delete model outputs, but you can improve source material.
  - Q: Where do I start?
    A: Run a 20-prompt baseline. Fix top three on-site gaps - About, FAQ, service clarity. Re-sample in 30 days and connect gaps to content tickets.

### A Practical Framework for Prioritizing Search Console Queries
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/gsc-query-prioritization-framework
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-02-12
- **Description:** Score Search Console queries by impressions, clicks, position and intent so your backlog reflects revenue instead of spreadsheet anxiety. Free framework.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: How many queries should I prioritize per week?
    A: Three shipped fixes maximum for small teams. More rarely completes; unfinished backlog demoralizes.
  - Q: Position or impressions - which matters more?
    A: Impressions show opportunity; clicks show reality. Near-miss bucket uses both - high impressions at position 8–15 is the sweet spot.
  - Q: Should branded queries go in bucket 1?
    A: Yes - protect branded clicks. But don't spend hours optimizing typos with 3 impressions.
  - Q: How do I handle seasonality?
    A: Compare year-over-year where possible. Rising shoulder-season queries in bucket 3 may need content 8–12 weeks before peak.
  - Q: Can this framework work for Greek and English queries?
    A: Yes - segment by language in GSC. Tag EL vs EN buckets separately for hreflang sites.

### Agency Playbooks - Delivery, Reporting, and Scaling Client SEO
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/pillar-agency-playbooks
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-02-01 · pillar hub

  - Q: What's a healthy agency client retention?
    A: When you ship visible work monthly and reports tie to their KPIs - 12–24 month tourism retainers are common with seasonal flex.
  - Q: Should agencies guarantee rankings?
    A: No - guarantee process: weekly ops, shipped fixes, transparent reporting. Rankings follow; guarantees create bad incentives.
  - Q: How do I pitch GEO/AEO without hype?
    A: Use LLM citations guide framing - directional sampling, not fake scores.
  - Q: White-label vs co-branded delivery?
    A: White-label software dashboards; co-branded thought leadership builds your authority. Match client preference.
  - Q: When to refer a project instead of taking it?
    A: YMYL without compliance reviewer, markets outside your expertise, clients who won't grant GSC access.

### AI & LLM Visibility - Measure What Models Say About Your Brand
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/pillar-ai-llm-visibility
- **Locale:** en · **Date:** 2026-02-01 · pillar hub
- **Description:** Pillar hub for generative search, citation tracking and building content that earns responsible mentions in AI answers from ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity.
- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: How is LLM visibility different from SEO?
    A: SEO measures rankings and clicks in search engines. LLM visibility measures whether AI assistants mention or cite your brand for category prompts. The levers overlap - clear content, strong entities, authoritative links - but the metrics differ.
  - Q: Should tourism brands prioritize GEO over local SEO?
    A: No. Map pack and organic traffic still drive most bookings for hotels and rent-a-car. GEO is additive. Fix GBP, citations, and location pages first; layer LLM tracking second.
  - Q: How often should we sample LLM outputs?
    A: Monthly for trend reporting; weekly for active campaigns or launches. Use the same prompts each time for comparability.
  - Q: Can AI-written content improve LLM visibility?
    A: Only if edited for accuracy and entity clarity. Unedited AI fluff rarely earns citations and can harm E-E-A-T. Use AI for drafts and scaling - not for publishing unchecked claims.
  - Q: Where do I start if I've never tracked this before?
    A: Run a 20-prompt baseline across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini. Fix the top three on-site gaps (about page, FAQ, service clarity). Re-sample in 30 days.

  - Q: Does local SEO still work?

  - Q: How much does local SEO cost?

### Google Business Profile Masterclass - Dominate Local Search
- **URL:** https://anotherseoguru.com/en/blog/google-business-profile-masterclass

- **Embedded FAQ:**
  - Q: How long until GBP optimization shows results?
    A: Category fixes and photo uploads often move within 2–4 weeks. Review velocity and posts compound over 60–90 days.
  - Q: Can I manage multiple locations in one dashboard?
    A: Yes - use Business Profile Manager for chains, hotel groups, and multi-desk rent-a-car operators.
  - Q: Do Google Posts affect rankings directly?
    A: Google doesn't confirm Posts as a core ranking factor, but they drive engagement signals and prove activity - especially vs dormant competitors.
  - Q: What if Google suspends my listing?

  - Q: Should I use a third-party GBP tool?
    A: Tools help scheduling and multi-location QA, but understand Google's policies. Over-automation without quality control hurts more than helps.

## 11. AnotherSEOGuru App documentation

The same guides are in Greek under https://anotherseoguru.com/el/help. Each page has a Markdown twin at its URL + ".md".

### What AnotherSEOGuru App does

> A tour of the product: your Search Console data, turned into a ranked list of fixes.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/getting-started/welcome

AnotherSEOGuru App reads your **Google Search Console** data and turns it into a weekly plan: which pages and queries to work on, what to change, and how many clicks each fix is likely to bring. Everything else in the product (keyword research, the site audit, content, competitors, AI visibility and client work) feeds that same plan.

![The This week screen in AnotherSEOGuru App with search performance, sales from Analytics and the sidebar navigation](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/overview-light.webp)
*This week is the home screen: how search is doing and what to fix first.*

## How it works

1. You sign in with Google and pick the Search Console properties you want to work on. Access is read-only.
2. We load up to 16 months of clicks, impressions, CTR and positions for each property.
3. The opportunity engine looks for queries close to page one, results with low CTR, pages losing traffic, pages competing with each other and topics you're missing.
4. Each finding becomes a fix with an estimated click impact. Send the ones you want to **Tasks**, ship them, and we measure the result.

## Where things are

| Area | What you do there |
| --- | --- |
| This week | The fixes worth the most clicks, search health and how traffic is trending. |
| Performance | Every query, page, country and device from Search Console, with comparisons. |
| Opportunities | Ranked fixes with estimated click impact. |
| Keywords and Content | Research, rank tracking, clusters, briefs, the writer and WordPress publishing. |
| Site audit | Crawl issues, indexability, Core Web Vitals and internal links. |
| Competitors and AI visibility | Keyword gap, backlinks, SERP explorer and how AI assistants mention you. |
| Agency | Clients, leads, pipeline, proposals, the client portal and reports. |

> **Tip:** Not ready to connect a site? Open the [live demo](https://app.anotherseoguru.com/demo). It runs on sample data for three fictional sites and every screen works.

## Moving around quickly

- Press `⌘K` (or `Ctrl K`) anywhere in the app to jump to any page, section or site.
- Use **Ask AI** in the top bar to ask questions about your own data in plain language.
- The site switcher at the top of the sidebar changes the property every screen works on.

![The command palette open over the app, with search results for keyword pages and sections](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/command-palette-light.webp)
*Press ⌘K to jump to any page, section or site.*

![The Ask AI panel open on the right, with suggested questions about the current site](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/ask-ai-light.webp)
*Ask AI answers questions from the data on the screen you're looking at.*

### Connect Google Search Console

> Sign in with Google, choose your properties and understand what we can and can't see.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/getting-started/connect-search-console

AnotherSEOGuru App works from your own Search Console data, so the first step is connecting the Google account that has access to your properties.

![The AnotherSEOGuru App sign-up page with the Continue with Google button](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/signup-light.webp)
*Create your account with Google to connect Search Console in one step.*

## Connect your account

1. Choose **Start with Google** on the sign-up page, or open **Settings → Integrations** if you're already signed in.
2. Pick the Google account that owns or has access to your Search Console properties.
3. Approve the read-only Search Console permission. We never ask for permission to change anything in your Google account.
4. Choose the properties you want to work on. Each one becomes a project.

![Settings, Integrations tab, showing Google, Search Console, Google Analytics 4 and WordPress as connected](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/settings-integrations-light.webp)
*Settings → Integrations shows which Google and WordPress connections are active.*

## Domain and URL-prefix properties

Both kinds work. A **domain property** (`sc-domain:example.com`) covers every subdomain and protocol, so it usually shows the most complete numbers. A **URL-prefix property** (`https://www.example.com/`) only covers URLs that start with that prefix. If you have both, use the domain property.

## How fresh the data is

Search Console reports with a delay of about 2–3 days, and the most recent days keep filling in for a while. Every dashboard shows **data through** the last complete day, and the note next to it tells you when we last refreshed. Search Console keeps 16 months of history, which is the longest range you can pick.

> **Note:** Only people with access to a property in Search Console can connect it. If a property is missing from the list, check in Search Console that this Google account has at least restricted access to it.

## Disconnecting

You can remove a project under **Projects**, or revoke our access at any time from your Google account's security settings. Revoking access stops all data loading straight away.

### Projects, brand terms and switching sites

> How projects work, why brand terms matter and how to manage many sites.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/getting-started/projects-and-sites

Each Search Console property you work on is a **project**. A project keeps the settings the rest of the product relies on: brand terms, competitors, the market you target and any linked client.

## What to set up first

- **Brand terms**: the names people use when they search for you. They split brand from non-brand demand, which is the traffic SEO work actually wins.
- **Competitors**: up to six sites you compete with. They power the keyword gap, backlinks, share of voice and AI visibility comparisons.
- **Market**: the country and language you target, used for keyword data and live results-page checks.

## Switching between sites

Use the site switcher at the top of the sidebar, or press `⌘K` and type the domain. **All sites** shows every project on one screen with its trend, drops, top movers and open fixes, which is the fastest way to see where to look first when you manage many sites.

![The All sites screen with click totals and a card for each site showing its trend, top mover and open fixes](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/portfolio-light.webp)
*All sites shows every project on one screen, sorted by the biggest drop.*

> **Tip:** Your plan sets how many projects you can have: 3 on Launch, 10 on Growth and 30 on Agency.

### A 10-minute weekly routine

> The quickest way to get value every week, step by step.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/getting-started/weekly-routine

Most of the value comes from doing a few things every week. Here's the routine we recommend.

1. Open **This week** and read the search health score and the metric tabs. Anything red is worth a look.
2. Go through **This week's fixes**. They're ordered by estimated clicks, so start at the top.
3. Send the fixes you agree with to **Tasks** with **Plan the push** or **Rewrite the title**.
4. Ship one or two of them. When a task is done, mark it shipped so we can measure it.
5. Check **Tasks → Results** for fixes shipped a few weeks ago and see what they earned.

## Once a month

- Run a **Site audit** and compare it with the previous crawl.
- Review **Rank tracking** and the rankings distribution for your most important keywords.
- If you report to someone, send a **Client report** for the month.

### The This week dashboard

> What each part of your home screen means and how to read it.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/search-performance/this-week

**This week** is your home screen. It answers three questions: how is search doing, what changed, and what should you do next.

![The This week dashboard with the site header, search performance summary and sales from Analytics](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/overview-light.webp)
*The This week dashboard for a sample site.*

## Search performance

The four tabs show clicks, impressions, CTR and average position for the selected range, with the change against the comparison period. Click a tab (or use the arrow keys) to chart that metric. Dotted markers on the chart are annotations: Google updates and changes you shipped.

## Search health and the ranking ladder

**Search health** is a 0–100 score built from click momentum, CTR against what your positions should earn, how much of your demand ranks in the top 10, and visibility growth. The **ranking ladder** counts your queries in the top 3, top 10, top 20 and top 100, and how many moved up or down.

## This week's fixes

The fixes worth the most clicks right now, ranked by estimated impact. Each one says what to do and why, and can go straight to your task list.

## Wins, risks and what people find you for

- **Biggest win** and **At risk** highlight the page that gained the most and the one losing the most.
- **What changed** lists the biggest click swings by query or page, and **Explain these changes** asks the AI assistant for likely causes.
- **What people find you for** shows your top queries and pages side by side, with average position and change.

### Queries, pages, countries and devices

> Explore every row Search Console returns, filter it and export it.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/search-performance/queries-and-pages

**Performance** is the full explorer for your Search Console data. Use the tabs for queries, pages, countries, devices and annotations, and the filters at the top to narrow everything to one device or country.

![Performance, Queries tab, with a table of queries showing clicks, impressions, CTR, position and detected opportunities](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/performance-queries-light.webp)
*Performance → Queries with quick filters and the opportunity column.*

## Filtering and quick filters

- Type in the filter box to match text. Wrap a pattern in slashes, like `/^how to/`, to use a regular expression.
- Quick filters pick common slices: brand or non-brand, new, lost, rising, falling and striking distance.
- Click any row to open its drawer with the trend, the matching pages or queries and suggested actions.

## How many rows you get

The query and page tables load up to **100,000 rows** per period, fetched from Search Console 25,000 at a time, so large sites over 16 months see their full long tail. Big ranges take a few seconds longer to load the first time.

> **Note:** Totals at the top come from Search Console's daily totals. They're usually higher than the sum of the rows because Google hides anonymized queries from row-level data.

## Exporting

Use **CSV** on any table to download exactly what you see, with the current filters, the comparison columns and any detected opportunity.

### Date ranges, comparisons and why numbers differ

> Pick ranges, compare periods and understand differences from other tools.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/search-performance/date-ranges

The date control in the top bar sets the range for every screen. You can pick a preset or a custom range, and choose what to compare it with: the previous period, the same period last year, or nothing.

## Days, weeks and months

Long ranges chart by week or month. When a week or month at the edge of the range is incomplete, we leave it out of the chart so a partial bucket doesn't look like a drop.

## Why numbers can differ

| You see | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Totals higher than the sum of rows | Anonymized queries are counted in totals but hidden from rows. |
| Slightly different numbers than Search Console | The newest days are still filling in. Refresh after a day or two. |
| Different positions than a live Google search | Search Console averages your top position across every search, weighted by impressions. |
| Lower numbers with a device or country filter | The filter also applies to the comparison period and the totals. |

### Annotations and measuring changes

> Mark what you shipped and Google's updates, then see their effect on the chart.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/search-performance/annotations

Annotations put context on your charts. Google algorithm updates are added for you, and you can add your own: a migration, a new section, a title rewrite.

1. Open **Performance → Annotations**, or choose **Annotate a change** under any chart.
2. Pick the date, write a short label and save.
3. The annotation shows as a marker on every chart that covers that date.

> **Tip:** Shipping a task from **Tasks** also records its ship date, so its before-and-after result is measured automatically.

### How opportunities are found and estimated

> The five detectors, how click impact is estimated and how to use the list.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/opportunities-tasks/opportunities

**Opportunities** looks at every query and page in your data and lists the changes most likely to bring more clicks. Each query or page appears once, under its biggest opportunity.

![The Opportunities screen with the potential clicks summary, detector tabs and the ranked list of fixes](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/opportunities-light.webp)
*Opportunities ranks every fix by estimated clicks per month.*

## The detectors

| Detector | What it finds | Typical fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Striking distance | Non-brand queries ranking 4–20 with real demand. | Strengthen the page and its internal links to reach the top 3. |
| Low CTR | Results on page one that earn far fewer clicks than their position usually gets. | Rewrite the title and meta description. |
| Content decay | Pages losing clicks compared with an earlier period. | Refresh the content and check what replaced you. |
| Cannibalization | Several of your pages competing for the same query. | Pick one page, merge or redirect the rest. |
| Missing content | Demand you get impressions for but have no good page for. | Write a dedicated page. |

![The Striking distance tab listing non-brand queries ranking 4 to 20 with their potential clicks and ranking page](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/striking-distance-light.webp)
*Striking distance: queries close to the top 3, with the clicks they could add.*

## How click impact is estimated

We compare where you rank today with the click-through rate a better position usually earns for that kind of query, and multiply by your impressions. It's an estimate of the size of the prize, not a promise, so use it to decide what to do first.

> **Note:** Content decay needs a comparison period. Turn one on in the date control to run that detector.

### Tasks, the board and measured results

> Keep every fix in one list, ship it and see what it earned.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/opportunities-tasks/tasks-and-results

**Tasks** holds every fix and follow-up, whether it came from an opportunity, the audit, a client request or you.

![The Tasks list with counters for in progress, due, overdue and done, and the open tasks below](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/tasks-light.webp)
*Tasks → List, filtered to all sites.*

## List, board and results

- **List** for sorting and filtering by status, priority, site or source.
- **Board** to move work from to-do to in progress to done.
- **Results** for shipped fixes, with the clicks and impressions before and after.

![The Tasks board with To do, In progress and Done & shipped columns](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/tasks-board-light.webp)
*Tasks → Board: drag a card to change its status.*

## How results are measured

When you mark a task shipped, we compare the page's Search Console data over the same number of days before and after the ship day, leaving the ship day itself out. We also measure the rest of your site over the same days as a control, so a sitewide rise or seasonal swing isn't credited to your fix.

![Tasks, Results tab, showing clicks gained from shipped fixes, a fix being measured and before-and-after results](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/tasks-results-light.webp)
*Tasks → Results: what each shipped fix earned, measured against the rest of the site.*

> **Tip:** Give a fix at least two to four weeks before judging it. Google needs time to recrawl and re-rank the page.

### Keyword research, collections and clusters

> Find keywords, save them and group them into topics.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/keywords-content/keyword-research

**Keywords → Research** shows search volume, difficulty, intent and the results page for any keyword in your market, alongside what you already rank for in Search Console.

![Keywords, Research tab, with the keyword search box, an assistant suggestion and keywords to start from](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/keywords-research-light.webp)
*Keywords → Research starts from the queries you already rank for.*

## Collections

Save keywords into collections to build a list for a campaign, a page or a client. You can expand a collection from seed keywords and brainstorm related ideas.

## Clusters and groups

- **Clusters** group keywords that the same page can rank for, so you plan one page per topic instead of one per keyword.
- **Groups** let you define your own segments (a product line, a location, a campaign) and follow their clicks and impressions together.

![Keywords, Clusters tab, with topic counts and a list of clusters showing clicks, impressions and average position](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/keywords-clusters-light.webp)
*Keywords → Clusters groups your Search Console queries into topics.*

> **Note:** Keyword research uses live data and costs credits per lookup. The cost is shown on the button before you run it.

### Rank tracking from Search Console

> Track daily positions for the keywords you care about, free.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/keywords-content/rank-tracking

Rank tracking follows the keywords you choose using Search Console's own data, so it's free and covers every device and country you rank in.

## How positions are measured

Each keyword's position is the average over the last 7 days, weighted by impressions, which is exactly how Search Console reports it. The 7d and 28d columns compare with the 7 days before and with 28 days earlier. Search Console updates daily with about a 3-day delay, and can differ from a single live check of Google.

## Rankings distribution

The card at the top splits your tracked keywords into Top 3, Page 1, Page 2, Page 3+ and Not ranking, and shows how many moved into or out of each tier in the last 28 days. Click a tier to filter the table to it.

![Keywords, Rank tracking tab, with the rankings distribution card and the tracked keywords table](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/keywords-tracking-light.webp)
*Rank tracking with the rankings distribution and 90-day trends.*

## Targets

Set a target position for a keyword to see how far it is from the goal. Keywords that are close to a target show up as suggestions for your next push.

### Briefs, the writer and WordPress publishing

> Go from a keyword to a published page.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/keywords-content/content-studio

**Content** covers the whole path from idea to published page.

![Content, Create tab, with page types, the target keyword field and the site style read from the client's site](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/content-create-light.webp)
*Content → Create: pick a page type and a keyword, and the draft follows the site's own style.*

| Tool | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| Create | Write a complete page (blog post, pillar page, hub or landing page) with schema and a preview. |
| Briefs | Plan a page: the questions to answer, the headings, the competitors that rank and the People Also Ask questions. |
| Optimizer | Score an existing page against the queries it ranks for and improve titles and copy. |
| Library | Import posts from WordPress or crawl any public site, keep version history and publish edits back. |
| FAQs and Products | Write FAQ answers and product descriptions with their structured data. |
| Templates | Set your house style and brand voice so every draft sounds like you. |

![Content, Briefs tab, with saved briefs and a brief showing length, sections, related terms and the outline](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/content-briefs-light.webp)
*Content → Briefs: the outline, terms and questions a page needs to cover.*

## Connect WordPress

1. In WordPress, create an application password under **Users → Profile**.
2. In AnotherSEOGuru App, open **Settings → Integrations** and add your site URL, username and application password.
3. Import posts and pages in **Content → Library**. Edits you make there can be published back with one click.

> **Warning:** Pages imported by crawl aren't linked to WordPress. To publish back, connect the site and import it from WordPress.

### Running a site audit

> Crawl your site, read the issues and compare crawls over time.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/site-audit/running-an-audit

**Site audit → Issues** crawls your site from the homepage and sitemap, checks every page for the problems that block rankings, and saves each crawl so you can compare them.

![Site audit, Issues tab, with the crawl history and what changed since the previous crawl](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/audit-issues-light.webp)
*Site audit → Issues with crawl history and a comparison with the previous crawl.*

## Crawl settings

- **Page limit**: how many pages one crawl covers. It depends on your plan; raise it in Settings when a crawl stops at the limit.
- **Render JavaScript**: for sites built with React, Vue, Wix and similar. **When needed** opens only the pages that look empty without JavaScript in a real browser.
- **Include sitemap**: also crawls pages from your XML sitemap and finds sitemap pages nothing links to.
- **Only crawl**: limits the crawl to one folder, like `/blog/`.

## Reading the results

Each crawled URL scores by its worst issue. Issues are grouped by area (indexing, content, links, social and structured data, performance) and each explains why it matters and how to fix it. Compare with an earlier crawl to see what's new and what you fixed.

> **Note:** Without JavaScript rendering, the crawler reads the HTML your server sends. Content added later by JavaScript isn't seen, and neither is it by AI assistants that only read plain HTML.

### Indexability, Core Web Vitals and internal links

> Find pages Google may not index, slow pages and weakly linked pages.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/site-audit/indexability-and-speed

## Indexability

The indexability report compares the pages Google shows in search with the URLs your site exposes. It finds pages that may not be indexed, pages missing from your sitemap and results that don't earn clicks. For Google's own answer on a URL, use **URL Inspection** in Search Console.

![Site audit, Indexability tab, with counts of discovered URLs and pages without impressions, and what to do about them](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/audit-indexability-light.webp)
*Site audit → Indexability compares what Google shows with what your site exposes.*

## Page speed

**Page speed** checks Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP and CLS) for your most important pages. Each metric uses field data from real Chrome users when Google has it for the URL, and the history shows the effect of a fix.

## Internal links

**Internal links** suggests links between your own pages based on their text: which page should link to which, the sentence where the link fits and the anchor text to use. Run a site crawl first so pairs that are already linked are hidden.

### The page inspector

> Check everything Google reads on a single page.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/site-audit/page-inspector

**Site audit → Page inspector** fetches any page and checks the on-page factors Google reads: status code, indexing directives, canonical, title tag, meta description, headings, links, images, structured data and Open Graph tags. It also shows the Search Console queries that page ranks for.

- Use it before and after publishing a change to confirm it's live.
- The preview shows roughly how the result looks on desktop. Google may rewrite titles and snippets.

> **Note:** Checks run on the HTML the server returns. HTTP headers such as `X-Robots-Tag` aren't visible here.

### Competitors, keyword gap and backlinks

> See how you compare, what they rank for that you don't and who links to them.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/competitors-ai/competitors

Add up to six competitors to a project. **Competitors** then shows how big each site is, your share of voice and where they're winning clicks you could get.

![The Competitors overview comparing keywords, estimated traffic and top 10 rankings, with share of voice](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/competitors-light.webp)
*Competitors → Overview with share of voice across tracked sites.*

## The tools

| Tool | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| Overview | Keywords, estimated traffic and top-10 rankings for you and each competitor, your share of voice and where you rank. |
| Keyword gap | Keywords competitors rank for and you don't, with volume and their positions. |
| Backlinks | Referring domains for you and each competitor, the anchor text they use, and sites that link to them but not to you. |
| Link building | Prospects and placements to track your outreach. |
| SERP explorer | Any Google results page the way searchers see it: who ranks and which features take the space. |
| Articles | Your competitors' strongest pages and an outline to beat them. |

> **Note:** Competitor numbers are estimates from our data partners, not Search Console data, so they're best for comparing sites with each other.

![Competitors, Keyword gap tab, with gap keywords, monthly searches, easy wins and the keywords to win table](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/competitors-gap-light.webp)
*Competitors → Keyword gap: what competitors rank for that you don't.*

### AI visibility: ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and AI Overviews

> Track whether AI assistants name you, and what to do about it.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/competitors-ai/ai-visibility

**AI visibility** shows how often AI assistants mention your brand when people ask the questions your customers ask, and how that compares with your competitors.

## What your own data shows

From Search Console and Google Analytics we show which of your pages appear in AI Overviews, queries where an AI Overview shows but you aren't cited, and visits that arrive from AI assistants.

![The AI visibility overview with AI Overview impressions, clicks from those queries and visits from AI assistants](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/ai-visibility-light.webp)
*AI visibility starts from what your own Search Console and Analytics data show.*

## The prompt tracker

1. Add the prompts you want to track, or describe a type of customer and we'll write the questions they'd ask.
2. Run a check. We ask each tracked engine and save every answer with its sources.
3. Read the results: mention rate per engine, share of voice and where you rank among the sites you track, and the prompts where a competitor is named and you aren't.

> **Tip:** Pages that get cited usually have current facts, a clear first paragraph that answers the question and named sources. The **Plan a fix** action on a missed prompt suggests exactly what to add.

### Local rankings

> See your Google Maps rank on a grid around your business.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/competitors-ai/local-rankings

**Local rankings** searches a keyword on Google Maps from every point of a grid around your business and records where you appear, so you can see how your local visibility changes street by street.

![Local rankings with tracked keywords, a grid of positions on the map and the share of points in the top 3](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/docs/web/local-light.webp)
*Local rankings: your Google Maps position at every point of the grid.*

1. Add your business as it appears on Google Business Profile.
2. Add the keywords you want to rank for, like `dentist near me`.
3. Run a scan. Each point on the map shows your position there; save scans to compare over time.

> **Warning:** Deleting a business also deletes its keywords and saved map scans. Credits already used aren't refunded.
