### Your data, privacy and Google access

> What we read, what we store and how to remove it.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/account-billing/privacy-and-data

- Google access is **read-only**. We can't change your Search Console settings or your site.
- Search Console data is used only for your own workspace and the clients you choose to share it with.
- Product analytics are optional. We ask once, and you can change your choice anytime from **Analytics preferences** (in the **More** menu on phones). We never send client domains, emails, prompts or report content.
- Remove a project under **Projects**. To delete your whole account and its data, write to support.

Read the [privacy policy](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/privacy) and our [security page](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/platform/security) for the details, or write to support@anotherseoguru.com with any question.

### Troubleshooting

> Fixes for the most common problems.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/account-billing/troubleshooting

### A dashboard shows no data

New properties take a day or two to show data in Search Console. Check the range isn't only the last 2–3 days, and that no device or country filter is active.

### A property is missing

Only properties the connected Google account can access appear. Add the account to the property in Search Console, then reload the list under **Projects**.

### "Create or select a project for this property first"

Every property needs a project before data loads. Add it under **Projects** or pick it in the site switcher.

### The audit says "Partial crawl"

The crawl stopped at your page limit, was stopped by you, or some pages couldn't be fetched. Raise the limit in crawl settings, or check that your site doesn't block crawlers.

### Numbers differ from Search Console

See [Date ranges, comparisons and why numbers differ](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/search-performance/date-ranges).

> **Tip:** Still stuck? Write to support@anotherseoguru.com with the page you were on and what you expected to see.

### Install the WordPress plugin

> Install AnotherSEOGuru 4.4.1 on WordPress, connect the site with OAuth, and publish title and description changes back with approval and undo.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/integrations/wordpress-plugin

AnotherSEOGuru for WordPress is a full SEO plugin from Touristas Technologies. Version **4.4.1** handles titles, meta descriptions, schema, XML sitemaps, redirects, breadcrumbs, `llms.txt`, IndexNow and on-page checks in English and Greek. Connecting a free AnotherSEOGuru App account at [app.anotherseoguru.com](https://app.anotherseoguru.com) adds Search Console in the editor, keyword research and AI titles. There is no API key to paste.

![AnotherSEOGuru dashboard in WordPress admin, score 35 of 100, two alerts, task list and site features](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/wp-dashboard.webp)
*Dashboard on a local WordPress site with plugin 4.4.1. The account is not connected, so Search Console stays empty. No tokens are shown.*

## What the plugin does

On its own, with no account, the plugin owns SEO for the site. The admin menu is **AnotherSEOGuru**, with Dashboard, Settings, Integrations, Tools, Redirects, Local SEO, Workouts, Help and Approvals.

- **Editor.** Snippet preview, up to five focus keywords (100 characters each), readability in English and Greek, SEO and readability columns on the posts list, and quick edit for the title and description.
- **Titles and meta.** Templates per post type, taxonomy, homepage, archives, search and the 404 page. Variables include `%%title%%`, `%%sitename%%`, `%%sep%%`, `%%sitedesc%%`, `%%excerpt%%`, `%%category%%` and `%%page%%`. The `%title%` style works too.
- **Front end, when no other SEO plugin is active.** Schema graph, Open Graph and X cards, XML sitemaps, breadcrumbs, `llms.txt`, IndexNow and extra `robots.txt` lines.
- **With an account.** Search Console numbers in the editor, keyword research (5 credits) and three AI title or description options (1 credit). Google Analytics 4 is viewed in AnotherSEOGuru App, not inside the WordPress editor.

> **Note:** If Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress or The SEO Framework is active, AnotherSEOGuru switches to companion mode. It prints nothing on the public site and writes titles into that plugin’s fields. Redirects and the 404 monitor start off.

## Requirements

| Requirement | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| WordPress | 6.2 or later. The plugin readme lists tested up to 6.9. |
| PHP | 7.4 or later. |
| Account link | The site must be served over **https**. WordPress only creates Application Passwords on https. |
| Who can connect | An administrator. Editors with `edit_others_posts` can open Approvals; only administrators change the approval switch. |
| Package | [anotherseoguru.zip](https://app.anotherseoguru.com/downloads/anotherseoguru.zip), version 4.4.1. |

## Install

1. **Download the zip** Get [anotherseoguru.zip](https://app.anotherseoguru.com/downloads/anotherseoguru.zip) from AnotherSEOGuru App. Do not rename the folder inside the zip.
2. **Upload it** In WordPress go to **Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin**, choose the zip and click **Install Now**.
3. **Activate** Click **Activate**. The first activation opens the setup wizard (the Dashboard route `/setup`).
4. **Open the menu** Use **AnotherSEOGuru** in the left admin menu. A search box labelled **Search settings** jumps to any screen.

## Connect the site to AnotherSEOGuru App

Connection is OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, scope `read tasks:write wordpress`. The consent screen names the client **AnotherSEOGuru for WordPress** plus your host. Older builds that asked you to paste an API key are not how 4.4.1 works.

![AnotherSEOGuru account screen in WordPress, status Not connected, with a Sign up free button](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/wp-account.webp)
*Integrations → AnotherSEOGuru account before a connection. The button is Sign up free. This capture uses a local site and no real account.*

1. **Open the account screen** Go to **AnotherSEOGuru → Integrations → AnotherSEOGuru account**. A disconnected site shows **Not connected**.
2. **Start the connection** Click **Sign up free**. WordPress sends you to app.anotherseoguru.com. AnotherSEOGuru App’s consent screen offers **Allow** or **Cancel**. Use the account you already have, or create one there.
3. **Let the plugin finish the link** After you allow access, the plugin creates a WordPress Application Password named **AnotherSEOGuru** and sends the site URL, username, that password and the plugin version to `POST /api/v1/wordpress/link`. You never copy the password yourself.
4. **Confirm the status** The screen then shows **Connected**, **Open your dashboard** and **Disconnect**. Disconnect deletes that Application Password and tells AnotherSEOGuru App to stop applying changes here.

> **Warning:** If the site is not on https, or a security plugin has turned Application Passwords off, the OAuth login can succeed and the link still fails. WordPress shows why: no Application Passwords in this WordPress version, https required, or Application Passwords turned off.

## Every settings screen

Settings live in the React admin, not in an old tabbed PHP page. Names below are the labels in version 4.4.1. Defaults are what a new install stores.

### Site features

![Site features in the WordPress plugin with XML sitemaps, schema, redirects, llms.txt, IndexNow and breadcrumbs switched on](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/wp-features.webp)
*Settings → Site features on a fresh install. Each switch is on.*

| Switch | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **XML sitemaps** | On | Publishes `/sitemap_index.xml` when the plugin is in standalone mode. |
| **Schema** | On | Prints the JSON-LD graph. |
| **Redirects** | On (off in companion mode) | Serves redirects from the plugin. |
| **llms.txt** | On | Publishes `/llms.txt`. |
| **Instant indexing** | On | IndexNow. A published or updated public URL can be submitted from the editor. |
| **Breadcrumbs** | On as a module; the trail itself starts off | Allows the breadcrumb functions. The trail is still off until you enable it under Breadcrumbs. |

### Site basics, representation and connections

![Site basics in the WordPress plugin with website name, title separator and homepage title template](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/wp-basics.webp)
*Settings → Site basics. The homepage template uses the variables sitename, page, sep and sitedesc.*

- **Website name** and **Alternate website name**.
- **Title separator**, used wherever a template contains `%%sep%%`.
- **This site represents** Organization or Person, plus the organization name or your name, and a square logo of at least 112 pixels.
- **Site connections.** Profiles for Facebook, X, Mastodon and other profiles. Webmaster verification codes for Google, Bing, Yandex, Pinterest, Baidu and Ahrefs.
- **Homepage** title template. A new site uses `%%sitename%% %%page%% %%sep%% %%sitedesc%%`.
- **Let search engines index this site** follows WordPress’s own “Search engine visibility” setting.
- **Restrict advanced settings for authors** hides advanced fields from authors.

### Content types, taxonomies and archives

Each public post type and taxonomy has its own screen. A new post type uses title `%%title%% %%page%% %%sep%% %%sitename%%` and description `%%excerpt%%`. Posts default to schema type BlogPosting and article type Article. Format archives start as noindex and out of the sitemap. Author, date and format archives, special pages, media pages and RSS each have a screen.

| Screen | What you set |
| --- | --- |
| **Media pages** | Enable media pages, show them in search results, show SEO controls, page type and article type. Media pages start disabled and noindex. |
| **RSS** | Text before and after each item. Variables include `%%AUTHORLINK%%`, `%%POSTLINK%%`, `%%BLOGLINK%%` and `%%BLOGDESCLINK%%`. |
| **Special pages** | Title templates for search results and the 404 page. |

### XML sitemaps

![XML sitemap settings with sitemaps and images on, news sitemap off, and 1000 entries per sitemap](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/wp-sitemaps.webp)
*Settings → XML sitemaps. Entries per sitemap defaults to 1000.*

| Setting | Default |
| --- | --- |
| **Generate XML sitemaps** | On |
| **Include images** | On |
| **News sitemap** | Off |
| **Entries per sitemap** | 1000 |
| **Exclude posts by ID** | Empty |

### Schema framework

**Output schema** turns the graph on (default on). The graph can include WebSite, Organization or Person, WebPage, BreadcrumbList and Article. Per-post types include Article, Product, Event, Recipe, Service, LocalBusiness and TouristTrip. A schema template can add one type to every item of a post type. FAQ and How-to blocks in the editor become FAQPage and HowTo structured data.

![Schema framework settings in the WordPress plugin](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/wp-schema.webp)
*Settings → Schema framework.*

### Crawl optimization and llms.txt

**Crawl optimization** can strip feeds, shortlinks, the generator tag, emoji scripts and other WordPress head noise. Search cleanup includes **Maximum characters in a search** (default 50) and **Allowed parameters**. **Extra lines** are appended to `robots.txt`.

AI crawlers you can block, one switch each: GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, CCBot, Bytespider, meta-externalagent, Amazonbot and AdsBot-Google.

![llms.txt settings in the WordPress plugin](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/wp-llms.webp)
*Settings → llms.txt. Publish llms.txt is on. Items per type defaults to 50.*

| llms.txt setting | Default |
| --- | --- |
| **Publish llms.txt** | On. The file is `/llms.txt`, and only while the plugin is in standalone mode. |
| **Items per type** | 50 |
| **File contents** | Auto (site name, description and main pages) or your own Markdown. |

### Breadcrumbs

The trail starts **off** even when the Site features module is on. Turn on **Enable breadcrumbs**. Other fields: separator (default `»`), anchor text for the homepage, prefix for the trail, prefix for archives, prefix for search pages, 404 page label, bold the last page, show on the homepage, show the blog page, and theme support. You can also use the shortcode `[asg_breadcrumbs]` or `do_action('asg_breadcrumbs')`.

### Redirects

![Empty redirects table in the WordPress plugin with type, code and target fields](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/wp-redirects.webp)
*AnotherSEOGuru → Redirects on a new site. Loop detection is on.*

- Codes: **301, 302, 307, 410, 451**. Match type: plain or regex (regex pattern up to 255 characters).
- Defaults: redirects enabled, 404 monitor on, log kept **30 days**, automatic slug redirect on, method PHP. In companion mode, redirects and the 404 monitor start off.
- The **404 log** lists hits. **Redirect settings** holds the switches above.

### Local SEO, integrations and tools

**Local SEO** (off until you enable the module) has Business details, Opening hours, Locations, Maps and Display. Business fields include address, phone, VAT, tax ID, currencies, payment methods and opening hours.

![WordPress integrations screen with several services marked Not available yet](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/wp-integrations.webp)
*Integrations. Several third-party switches are labelled Not available yet in 4.4.1. Do not treat those as working connections.*

- **Tools → Import and export.** Bring in Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, and redirects from the Redirection plugin. Run a dry run first. Old data in the other plugin is not deleted.
- **Tools → File editor** and **Bulk editor**.
- **Tools → SEO data optimization** stores the scores used by the posts list.
- **Workouts** include a cornerstone workout and an orphaned-content workout.
- Ahrefs on this screen is a verification code you can save. Semrush, SEOTesting, rank tracking inside WordPress, Elementor, WooCommerce, TranslatePress, custom fields, Jetpack and Site Kit are marked **Not available yet**.

![Import and export screen with Yoast, Rank Math, AIOSEO, SEOPress and Redirection listed as not detected](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/wp-import.webp)
*Tools → Import and export on a site that has none of those plugins. The settings backup download and restore are on the same screen.*

## Two-way sync with AnotherSEOGuru App

Once the site is linked, AnotherSEOGuru App reads published content from WordPress and writes titles and descriptions back through the same plugin. The plugin is the place that applies, holds or undoes a change. This guide does not name buttons inside AnotherSEOGuru App, because those labels are not in the plugin package.

1. **AnotherSEOGuru App reads published items** WordPress exposes `GET /wp-json/asg/v1/seo-index`. The default post type is page. Only **published** items are included, newest modified first, up to **100** per page. Each item returns the post id, URL, post type, and the raw SEO title and description. Callers who cannot edit that post are skipped.
2. **A write goes through the change log** `POST /wp-json/asg/v1/seo` and `POST /wp-json/asg/v1/seo-bulk` set the title, the description, or both. Every write stores the previous value. If **Require approval** is on, the write stays pending instead of going live.
3. **A conditional write checks the page has not moved** `POST /wp-json/asg/v1/seo-change` is stricter. The post must be published, the field must be title or description, and the expected snapshot version must still match. If someone edited the page after the preview, WordPress refuses the write so an old suggestion cannot overwrite a newer one.
4. **Applied changes are sent back** Applied rows are posted to AnotherSEOGuru App at `POST /api/v1/wordpress/changes`, up to 20 per request, with the site URL. The log itself stays in WordPress (option `asg_change_log`, newest 200 rows).

> **Tip:** Task sync runs at most every 300 seconds. Opening a plugin screen or the post editor also syncs when the account is connected. Search Console numbers shown in the editor are cached for one minute.

## Approvals, history and undo

![WordPress Approvals screen with require-approval unchecked, SEO tools on, and empty waiting and change-log tables](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/wp-approvals.webp)
*AnotherSEOGuru → Approvals on a local site. The domain line shows the authorized host and this site. Nothing is waiting, so both tables say Nothing here yet.*

Open **AnotherSEOGuru → Approvals**. Editors can review. Administrators also see the switches.

| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Authorized domain** | Writes are refused when the current host is not the authorized one (a copied or staging site). An administrator uses **Re-authorize this domain** to allow this host. |
| **Require approval before the app, MCP or chat can change SEO** | Off by default. On, those writes wait in **Waiting for approval**. |
| **SEO tools** | Each tool can be On or off: List content, Read SEO, Update SEO, Read schema, Update schema, List redirects, Create redirect, Update redirect, Delete redirect, Suggest internal links, Insert internal link. |

Both tables use the columns **When, Who, Change, Before, After, Status**. Who is the actor (`app`, `mcp`, `user` or `chat`) plus the login when there is one. Buttons:

- **Approve** or **Reject** on a pending row.
- **Undo** on an applied row that has not already been undone. Undo writes the previous value back.
- **Publish draft** when a row is a draft preview.

**SEO chat** on the same screen asks AnotherSEOGuru App for a title or description. The prompt says: “Ask the AnotherSEOGuru app for a title or description. Suggestions wait in the list above until you approve them.” Page ID is optional. The message can be up to 2000 characters. Suggestions are stored as approvals. They are not published by the chat form itself.

> **Note:** The plugin does not edit a page-builder layout. Title, description, schema and the other SEO tools above are the writes it will apply.

## On a page or post

The block editor and the classic editor both get an AnotherSEOGuru panel.

- **Focus keywords.** Up to five, each up to 100 characters, stored as `_asg_focus_keywords`. Checks cover the title, description, URL, introduction, subheadings, image alt text, density, length and links.
- **Snippet length.** The preview measures pixels. Desktop titles are flagged around 580 pixels (a short title under about 300). Mobile titles use about 540. Descriptions use about 920 desktop and 680 mobile.
- **Keyword research** calls AnotherSEOGuru App and costs **5 credits**. **AI meta** returns three options and costs **1 credit**. If the account is out of credits the editor says to add credits in AnotherSEOGuru.
- **Connected changes** in the editor is the same task and approval history. Refresh to see the latest status.
- The posts list can show SEO and readability scores, and quick edit can set the title, description and noindex.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Account stays **Not connected** | Finish **Sign up free** and choose Allow on AnotherSEOGuru App. If you closed the window, start again from Integrations → AnotherSEOGuru account. |
| Connected, but the link failed | The site must be https, and Application Passwords must be available for your user. A security plugin can turn them off. |
| Writes do nothing on a staging copy | Approvals shows a domain mismatch. Use **Re-authorize this domain** only on the copy you mean to edit. |
| A title from AnotherSEOGuru App never appears | Open **Waiting for approval**. If approval is required, click **Approve**. If the page changed after the preview, the conditional write is refused and AnotherSEOGuru App has to send a fresh one. |
| **Undo** is missing | Undo is only on a row whose status is applied and that has not already been undone. |
| No sitemap or schema on the public site | Another SEO plugin is active, so this one is in companion mode and prints nothing on the front end. Or the matching switch under Site features is off. |
| Import found nothing | Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress or Redirection has to be installed. The import screen says **Not detected** when it is not. |

## FAQ

**Do I paste an API key into the plugin?**

No. Version 4.4.1 connects with OAuth. The plugin creates an Application Password named AnotherSEOGuru and sends it to AnotherSEOGuru App. You do not copy a key.

**Does the plugin work without an account?**

Yes. Titles, schema, sitemaps, redirects, breadcrumbs, llms.txt and the on-page checks work with no account. Search Console, keyword research and AI titles need the connection.

**Will it replace Yoast or Rank Math?**

Only if you want it to. While another SEO plugin is active, AnotherSEOGuru stays in companion mode, writes into that plugin’s fields, and does not print its own tags. Import copies data across and leaves the old data in place.

**Where do I approve a change before it goes live?**

AnotherSEOGuru → Approvals. Turn on Require approval before the app, MCP or chat can change SEO. Pending rows have Approve and Reject. Applied rows have Undo.

**How far back does the change log go?**

The plugin keeps the newest 200 rows in WordPress. Undo is available on an applied row until you undo it or the row ages out of that list.

**Which content is imported into AnotherSEOGuru App?**

The index endpoint returns published posts and pages (and any other public post type you request), with the current SEO title and description. Drafts are not in that index.

### Install the Chrome extension

> Install AnotherSEOGuru 3.2.2 for Chrome, audit any page in the browser, and sign in to see Search Console data for that page.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/integrations/chrome-extension

AnotherSEOGuru for Chrome is a Manifest V3 extension, version **3.2.2**. It audits the page you are on, entirely in the browser, and shows a score, a Google snippet preview and the fixes. Sign in and the same popup adds that page’s Search Console numbers from your account. The package has no Chrome Web Store URL. You install it from the zip.

![AnotherSEOGuru Chrome extension popup on the Overview tab, score 96, signed out](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/ext-overview.webp)
*Overview on https://anotherseoguru.com/en, signed out. The audit ran in the browser. Score 96 is this capture of that page, not a target.*

## What the extension does

- **Popup and side panel.** The toolbar icon opens the popup. **Open in side panel** keeps the same audit beside the page. Shortcut **Alt+Shift+S** (also on Mac).
- **Five tabs:** Overview, Audit, Content, Technical and My data.
- **On-page checks with no account.** Title length, meta description, headings, content, canonical, indexability, structured data, Open Graph and Core Web Vitals measured in the page.
- **Signed in.** Clicks, impressions, CTR and average position for this URL, quick wins, open tasks, and keyword research. Those calls go to AnotherSEOGuru App at app.anotherseoguru.com. Everything else stays on your computer.
- **Google results.** On Google search only, position badges and your sites. Optional SEO bar on other sites, off until you turn it on.

> **Note:** The on-page audit is free without an account and runs locally in your browser. That line is in the extension itself, under the sign-in button.

## Requirements

| Requirement | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Browser | Chrome **116** or later (Manifest V3, `minimum_chrome_version`). |
| Permissions always on | `activeTab`, `scripting`, `storage`, `identity`, `contextMenus`, `sidePanel`. |
| Sites it may read without asking again | Google search on google.com, google.gr and google.co.uk, for the results overlay. |
| Optional permission | `<all_urls>`, asked only when you turn the SEO bar on. |
| Package | [anotherseoguru-extension.zip](https://app.anotherseoguru.com/downloads/anotherseoguru-extension.zip), version 3.2.2. |

## Install from the zip

1. **Download and unzip** Get [anotherseoguru-extension.zip](https://app.anotherseoguru.com/downloads/anotherseoguru-extension.zip) and unzip it. Keep the folder that contains `manifest.json`.
2. **Open Chrome’s extensions page** Go to `chrome://extensions`.
3. **Turn on Developer mode** Use the **Developer mode** switch on that page.
4. **Load the folder** Click **Load unpacked** and choose the unzipped folder. The name in Chrome is **AnotherSEOGuru App: SEO checker & Search Console**.
5. **Pin it** Pin AnotherSEOGuru from the puzzle-piece menu so the toolbar icon stays visible. Click it, or press **Alt+Shift+S**.

## Sign in to AnotherSEOGuru App

Sign-in is OAuth. The client name is **AnotherSEOGuru for Chrome**. The scope is `read tasks:write`. The extension registers itself, sends you to `https://app.anotherseoguru.com/connect`, and stores the tokens in the browser. There is no API key field.

![My data tab of the Chrome extension signed out, with an example clicks chart marked Example](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/ext-my-data.webp)
*My data while signed out. The sparkline is labelled Example · clicks, 28 days. It is a sample, not live Search Console data.*

1. **Open My data** Click the toolbar icon, then the **My data** tab.
2. **Sign in** Click **Sign in with AnotherSEOGuru**. A second button, **Sign up free**, opens `https://app.anotherseoguru.com/auth?mode=signup` if you do not have an account yet.
3. **Allow the connection** Approve **AnotherSEOGuru for Chrome** on AnotherSEOGuru App. When it returns, the tab shows **Signed in as** your name or email, your plan, credits and site count, plus **Open app** and **Sign out**.
4. **Use it on your own site** Search Console numbers load only when the page’s host is a site on your account. On any other host the tab says the page is not one of your sites and links to **Add a site** (`/app/sites`).

## How it works on a page

Open a normal website, then the popup. Chrome’s own pages, the Web Store and local files cannot be analyzed. The popup says **Open a web page** in that case. If the side panel has no access yet it says **Allow this tab**.

### Overview

Overview shows one score and the main issues. Bands are **good** at 80 or above, **ok** from 50 to 79, and **poor** below 50. The capture above is a 96 on the public English homepage, signed out.

### Audit

![Audit tab of the Chrome extension listing on-page checks for anotherseoguru.com](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/ext-audit.webp)
*Audit tab for the same page. Checks run locally. Length rules are 30 to 60 characters for the title and 70 to 160 for the meta description.*

Groups are On-page, Content, Technical, and Schema & social. A title under 30 or over 60 characters is flagged, and a meta description under 70 or over 160. Fewer than 300 words is marked thin. The same rules drive the score.

### Content

![Content tab of the Chrome extension with the Google snippet preview](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/ext-content.webp)
*Content tab: the snippet preview and the content checks for the open page.*

### Technical

![Technical tab of the Chrome extension showing Core Web Vitals measured in the browser](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/ext-tech.webp)
*Technical tab. LCP, CLS, FCP, TTFB and INP are read from the page when the browser has them.*

Pass lines, in milliseconds except CLS: LCP good under 2500 and poor over 4000, CLS good under 0.1 and poor over 0.25, FCP good under 1800 and poor over 3000, TTFB good under 800 and poor over 1800, INP good under 200 and poor over 500. A missing metric is skipped.

### My data, once you are signed in

On a site that belongs to the account, My data loads page insights from AnotherSEOGuru App:

- **Search performance.** Clicks, impressions, CTR and average position, labelled **Last 28 days vs previous**, plus a daily-clicks chart when AnotherSEOGuru App returns daily rows.
- **Top queries.** Up to eight queries, with clicks, impressions and position.
- **Quick wins.** Queries in positions **8 to 20** with at least **10** impressions, at most five. The extra-clicks figure is an estimate of a move to position 3. The note under the list says so.
- **Open tasks** for the page, and **Send issues** to the task board. **Open in app** goes to AnotherSEOGuru App.
- **Keyword research.** The pill says **5 credits**. Results show volume, difficulty, CPC, ideas and questions. If the response reports no credits used, the extension says **Repeat search: no credits used.**

If Search Console is not connected for that site, the tab says so and links you to connect it. Insights are cached in the browser for 10 minutes. Score history is local only: up to 40 points per page and 300 pages (`asg_history`).

### Report, bulk check and the SEO bar

- **Full report** opens a printable report of the same audit. The footer reads “Made with AnotherSEOGuru”.
- **Bulk check URLs** checks up to **50** pages at once.
- The **SEO bar** is a strip at the top of a page (score, title, description, H1, word count). It is **off** until you enable it, and enabling it asks Chrome for access to all sites.

## Every setting

Open the gear icon. The sheet title is **Settings**. Defaults are listed as they are stored.

![Settings sheet of the Chrome extension with theme, language, Google overlay, toolbar badge and SEO bar](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/help/ext-settings.webp)
*The real settings sheet, expanded so every control is in the frame. Values are the defaults: System, Auto, overlay on, Full, Clicks, SEO bar off.*

| Setting | Choices | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Theme** | System, Light, Dark | System |
| **Language** | Auto, English, Greek | Auto (follows the browser) |
| **Show on Google results** | On or off. Subtitle: position numbers, your sites and your Search Console numbers. | On |
| **Overlay style** | Full, Compact, Minimal. Compact starts the toolbar folded. Minimal shows the numbers only. | Full |
| **Toolbar badge** | Clicks, Open tasks, or Off. Shown on pages of your own sites. | Clicks |
| **SEO bar on every page** | On or off. Asks for access to all sites. | Off |
| **Clear local data** | Removes score history, remembered Google results and sent-task marks. You stay signed in and settings stay. | Button |

The sheet also shows the shortcut and a **Privacy** link. That link opens `https://anotherseoguru.com/en/privacy`. **Clear local data** deletes `asg_history`, `asg_sent_tasks`, `asg_serps`, `asg_section` and `asg_serp_badges`. It does not delete the sign-in or `asg_settings`.

## On a Google results page

The results helper is a content script on `google.com/search`, `google.gr/search` and `google.co.uk/search` only. With **Show on Google results** on, it adds position badges, a small export toolbar and, when you are signed in, a highlight on your own sites. Turning the overlay off removes it immediately. Compact and Minimal change how much of that toolbar you see. A CSV export is part of the same toolbar.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| **Open a web page** | You are on a Chrome page, the Web Store, or a local file. Switch to an https site and click the icon again. |
| **Allow this tab** | The side panel does not have access yet. Click **Allow this tab**, or click the toolbar icon on that tab (that uses the activeTab permission). |
| **Couldn't read this page** | Reload the page and open the popup again. |
| My data still shows the example chart | You are signed out. The chart is labelled **Example · clicks, 28 days**. Use **Sign in with AnotherSEOGuru**. |
| Signed in, but no Search Console numbers | The host is not a site on the account, or Search Console is not connected for it. Use **Add a site** or the connect link in the tab. Numbers are for your sites only. |
| SEO bar never appears | It ships off. Turn on **SEO bar on every page** and accept the all-sites permission Chrome asks for. |
| Google results have no badges | **Show on Google results** is off, or you are not on google.com, google.gr or google.co.uk search. |
| Sign-in expired | The extension clears the session on an unauthorized response and asks you to sign in again. |

## FAQ

**Is the extension in the Chrome Web Store?**

The 3.2.2 package does not include a store URL. Install it with Load unpacked from anotherseoguru-extension.zip.

**Does the audit send my page to AnotherSEOGuru App?**

No. Title, content, schema and vitals checks run in the browser. Only a signed-in session calls AnotherSEOGuru App, and only for account data: page insights, tasks, keyword research, AI meta and results insights.

**What does signing in allow?**

The OAuth scope is read and tasks:write, under the client name AnotherSEOGuru for Chrome. You can read your sites and send tasks. The extension does not receive an API key to paste.

**Why is the chart on My data not my traffic?**

Signed out, that chart is a sample. The label is Example · clicks, 28 days, and it is hidden from assistive tech. Sign in and open one of your own URLs to see live numbers.

**Where is score history kept?**

In this browser only, up to 40 scores per page and 300 pages. Clear local data removes it. Sign-in and settings stay.

**Can I use it in Greek?**

Yes. Settings → Language → Greek, or Auto when the browser is Greek. The extension ships English and Greek strings.

### Get the iPhone beta

> The iPhone app is in beta through Apple's TestFlight. Here's how to request an invite and install it.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/get-the-beta

AnotherSEOGuru App for iPhone is a native app (not a web view) on the same account and data as the web app. It's in **beta through Apple's TestFlight**. It isn't on the App Store yet, so the only way to install it is with a TestFlight invite from us.

## What you need

- An iPhone on **iOS 17 or later**. On iOS 26 and later the app uses the system's Liquid Glass tab bar.
- The free **TestFlight** app from Apple.
- An AnotherSEOGuru App account, or none at all: the app has a sample workspace you can explore before you connect anything.

## Request an invite and install

1. **Email us for access** Write to [support@anotherseoguru.com](mailto:support@anotherseoguru.com?subject=iPhone%20beta%20access) with the subject **iPhone beta access**. Use the email address you want the invite sent to (it doesn't have to be your AnotherSEOGuru App login).
2. **Install TestFlight** On your iPhone, install **TestFlight** from the App Store. It's Apple's own app for beta testing.
3. **Accept the invite** Open the invite email (or the invite link we send) on your iPhone and tap through to TestFlight. Tap **Accept**, then **Install**.
4. **Open the app and sign in** AnotherSEOGuru appears on your Home Screen. Sign in with the same account you use on the web, or tap **Explore the sample workspace**. See [Sign in and sync](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/sign-in-and-sync).

> **Note:** The app on your Home Screen is called **AnotherSEOGuru**. It's the iPhone version of AnotherSEOGuru App, on the same account, plan and credits.

## Getting new builds

We ship beta builds often. TestFlight tells you when one is ready: open **TestFlight → AnotherSEOGuru → Update**. Your data lives on your account, not in the build, so updating never loses projects or tasks. Each beta build expires after a while; when TestFlight says a build has expired, install the latest one from the same screen.

> **Tip:** Found a bug or something confusing? Reply to us at support@anotherseoguru.com with a screenshot and what you expected to happen. Beta feedback goes straight into the next build.

### Sign in and sync with the web app

> Use the same AnotherSEOGuru App account on your iPhone. What syncs, what stays on the device and how to switch language.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/sign-in-and-sync

The iPhone app signs in to the **same account** as app.anotherseoguru.com. There's no separate subscription or setup: your projects, plan, credits and tasks are already there.

![The AnotherSEOGuru sign-in screen on iPhone with Continue with Apple, Continue with Google, Continue with email, the sample workspace link and the Clients Area](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/iphone/sign-in.webp)
*The first screen: sign in with Apple, Google or email, try the sample workspace, or open the Clients Area.*

## Ways to sign in

## Connecting Search Console

1. **Tap Connect with Google** If your account has no Google connection yet, the app asks for one after you sign in. Access is read-only: the app reads Search Console and Analytics and never changes anything in your Google account.
2. **Approve on Google's page** Pick the Google account that has access to your properties and approve. You're sent back to the app.
3. **If the app doesn't notice** If you finished on Google but the app still waits, tap **I've connected it on the website**.

If Google stops accepting an old connection, **Settings → Google** shows **Needs reconnecting**. Tap **Reconnect Google** to fix it.

| Synced with your account | Saved on this iPhone only |
| --- | --- |

| Plan, credits and recent credit activity |  |

## Greek and English

The whole app is available in English and Greek. Go to **Settings → Language** and choose **English**, **Ελληνικά** or **Same as iPhone**. The choice is saved to your account, so emails and notifications from us use the same language.

## Signing out and deleting your account

**Settings → Sign out** removes the account from this iPhone and stops its notifications and Lock Screen activities. **Settings → Delete my account** deletes the account and its data for good, as Apple requires. If your plan still renews, cancel it in Billing first so you're not charged afterwards.

### Today and this week's fixes

> Read the Today tab, act on this week's fixes and measure them in Work.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/today

**Today** is the first tab and the iPhone version of the web app's This week screen. It answers three questions in one scroll: how search is doing, what changed and what to do next. The site pill above the tab bar shows which site you're looking at; tap it to switch.

![The Today tab on iPhone with a Search health score of 86 of 100, clicks, pages up and fixes, and the search performance cards](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/iphone/today.webp)
![The Ranking ladder on iPhone with Top 3, Top 10, Top 20 and Top 100 tiles and a Needs attention list](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/iphone/ranking-ladder.webp)

## What's on the screen

| Section | What it tells you |
| --- | --- |
| **Search health** | One 0–100 score from your Search Console query rows: click momentum, CTR vs expected, top-10 reach and visibility growth. Tap it for **How the score is built**. |
| Clicks, Pages up, Fixes | The period's clicks, how many pages gained and how many fixes are waiting. |
| **Search performance** | Clicks, impressions, CTR and average position against the previous 28 days. |
| **Do these first** | The fixes worth the most clicks right now, with **Add to Tasks** and **Ask**. |
| **Biggest win** and **At risk** | The page that gained the most and the one losing the most. |
| **Ranking ladder** | How many searches rank in the top 3, 10, 20 and 100, and how many moved up or down. Tap a tile to see the searches that entered or left that band. |
| **Needs attention** | Drops, decaying pages and Google updates. **See all** opens Alerts. |
| **Top movers** | The searches that gained or lost the most clicks. |

> **Note:** The line under the score says which dates you're seeing, for example **Data through Oct 10**. Search Console reports with a delay of about two days. Tap the **i** for the reporting period, the comparison period and when the data was last refreshed.

## Turn a fix into a result

1. **Add the fix to your tasks** Tap **Add to Tasks** on a fix in **Do these first**, or open **Work → Fixes** for the full list. Sort by **Biggest impact**, **Least effort** or **Newest**, and filter by kind: striking distance, low CTR, decay, cannibalization or missing content.
2. **Do the work** Open the task in **Work → Tasks**. **Ask the assistant how to do it** writes the finished text, such as a new title, for that page.
3. **Mark it shipped** Tap **Mark shipped**, pick the day the change went live, what to measure (the page, one search query or the whole site) and how long: 14, 28 or 56 days.
4. **Read the verdict** When the window closes, the task moves to **Work → Results** as **Won**, **Flat** or **Lost**. A win means clicks rose at least 10% and by more than normal day-to-day swings.

> **Tip:** Pull down on Today to refresh. The app uses the same opportunity engine and measuring rules as the web app, so both list the same fixes for the same site. Tasks you add on the phone show up on the web straight away.

### Search performance on iPhone

> Open any search or page in detail, change dates and compare periods, and read GA4 traffic acquisition.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/search-performance

The **Insights** tab holds your reports. Its three segments are **Search Console**, **Analytics** and **AI evidence**. This article covers the first two; AI evidence has [its own guide](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/ai-visibility).

## Searches, pages, countries and devices

The Search Console segment is the full report: searches, pages, countries and devices, sortable and filterable, with share-of-clicks bars. Use the calendar button to pick **Last 7 days** up to **Last 16 months**, or a **Custom range**, and compare with the **Previous period**, the **Same period last year** or nothing.

- Filter with **Contains**, or switch to **Regex** for a Search Console regular expression. The app warns you about patterns Google doesn't support, such as lookahead.
- The **Search** tab (the magnifying glass in the tab bar) finds fixes, searches, pages and tasks for the selected site in one place.

## One search in detail

Tap any search or page to open its detail screen.

![The detail screen for one search on iPhone with clicks, impressions, CTR and position tabs, a chart against the previous period and buttons for Track rank, SERP explorer, Start content and Ask the assistant](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/iphone/search-detail.webp)
*One search over the last 28 days: metric tabs, the chart against the previous period with Google updates marked, and the next steps.*

| Part | What you can do |
| --- | --- |
| Metric tabs | Switch the chart between **Clicks**, **Impressions**, **CTR** and **Position**. A dashed line is the previous period; dots mark Google updates. |
| **Track rank** | Add the search to rank tracking. The same tracked keywords appear on the web. |
| **SERP explorer** | See the live Google top 10 for this search. See [Keywords and rankings](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/keywords-and-rankings). |
| **Start content** | Open the Content writer with the search copied, ready to paste. |
| **Ask the assistant** | Open the assistant with a question about this search already filled in. |
| Fixes and pages | Any fix in this week's plan for the search, and the pages that rank for it with their own clicks, CTR and position. |

## Traffic acquisition from GA4

The **Analytics** segment reads your Google Analytics 4 property. Connect Analytics with the same read-only Google access, then tap **Link a GA4 property** to pair it with this site.

![The Traffic acquisition report on iPhone splitting sessions into organic search, paid ads, AI assistants, direct, other websites, social, email and other referrals](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/iphone/traffic-acquisition.webp)
*Traffic acquisition: every GA4 session grouped by channel, with AI assistants as a channel of their own.*

Traffic acquisition groups sessions into **Organic search**, **Paid ads**, **AI assistants**, **Direct**, **Other websites**, **Social**, **Email** and **Other referrals**, each with a plain-language explanation. **Daily traffic** charts sessions over time, and **Export CSV** saves the rows.

> **Warning:** A fresh Analytics report costs **2 credits**; a cached one is free for an hour. GA4 sessions and Search Console clicks are different measures, so the app never adds them together.

### Keywords, rankings and the SERP explorer

> Research a keyword, track its position and check who gets the clicks on the live results page.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/keywords-and-rankings

The keyword tools live under **Workspace → Growth** and **Workspace → Market**. Tap **Find a tool** to search for one, and star the ones you use most to keep them under **Favorite tools**.

## Keyword research

![Keyword research for mykonos villas on iPhone with 720 monthly searches, keyword difficulty 13, CPC, competition, intent and a 12-month search volume trend](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/iphone/keyword-research.webp)
*Keyword research: volume, difficulty, intent and a 12-month trend for any search in any market.*

1. **Pick a search** Start from one of your top Search Console searches, or type any keyword. Choose the market (country and language).
2. **Read the overview** You get **Search volume** per month and its recent change, keyword difficulty (KD), **CPC**, **Competition**, the number of results and the **Intent**: informational, navigational, commercial or transactional.
3. **Check the trend and ideas** **Search volume trend** shows monthly searches for the last 12 months. Below it are **Related searches**, questions people ask and keyword ideas. Tap one for its own overview, or hold it for actions.
4. **Act on it** **Track rank** adds the keyword to rank tracking, **Add task** puts it on your list, and the sparkle button asks the assistant about it.

> **Warning:** Keyword data and the SERP explorer use credits. Before any paid check the app shows **Review the credit cost** with the price and your balance. Only a completed result is charged; saved results are free.

## Rank tracking and the ranking ladder

**Rank tracking** shows your tracked keywords with their daily Google position, best position and 7-day movement. Positions come from Search Console and update daily, about two days behind. Tracked keywords are shared with the web app, so adding or removing one on the phone changes it everywhere.

For the bigger picture, the **Ranking ladder** on [Today](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/today) counts every search in the top 3, 10, 20 and 100 and how many moved.

## SERP explorer

![The SERP explorer on iPhone for seajets cancellations today in Greece, English, showing your position, results, ads, AI Overview cited, SERP features and a donut chart of who gets the clicks](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/iphone/serp-explorer.webp)
*SERP explorer: your position, the SERP features on the page and the expected share of clicks for each site in the top 10.*

1. Open **SERP explorer** from a search's detail screen, or from Workspace, and type the search.
2. Pick the market, for example **Greece · English**, and tap **Check**.
3. Read **Your position**, the number of results and ads, and whether the **AI Overview** cites you.
4. **SERP features** lists what's on the page, such as AI Overview and **People Also Ask**. **Who gets the clicks** estimates each site's share of organic clicks in the top 10.

Scroll down for the full AI Overview text with its sources, the **People Also Ask** questions to answer on your page, and the organic results. More on AI Overviews in [AI visibility](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/ai-visibility).

### Site audit on iPhone

> Start a crawl, leave the app and follow it on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/site-audit-on-iphone

The **Site audit** crawls your site for technical problems that hold rankings back, then lists them in order of severity. Open it from **Workspace → Technical health**.

## Run an audit

1. **Open Site audit** Make sure the right site is selected in the site pill, then open **Workspace → Site audit**.
2. **Choose how many pages** Set **Pages to crawl** and tap **Run audit** (or **Run a new audit** if you've run one before). The audit uses credits, so the app shows the cost first.
3. **Leave the screen if you like** The audit moves from **Queued** to **Crawling** to **Analyzing**. You can go to another tab or lock your phone: the crawl keeps running and its results appear in Site audit when it's done.

![Site audit on iPhone crawling discovercyclades.gr, 0 of up to 10 pages, with Queued, Crawling and Analyzing steps](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/iphone/site-audit.webp)
*A crawl in progress. You can leave this screen; the audit keeps running and shows up when it's done.*

## Progress on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island

While an audit runs, a **Live Activity** shows its progress outside the app, even when the app is in the background:

| Where | What you see |
| --- | --- |
| Lock Screen | The site, a progress bar and a status line such as pages crawled out of the limit. When it finishes: the **Health** score with the number of critical issues and warnings. |
| Dynamic Island (compact) | An icon for the current phase and the crawled pages, for example `12/50`, then the score when done. |
| Dynamic Island (expanded) | Touch and hold to see the site, the progress bar and the status line. |

Tap the Live Activity to open the Site audit for that site. When the crawl finishes you get **Audit ready, tap to see results**. Only one audit is shown at a time; starting a new crawl replaces the old one.

> **Note:** If the Live Activity hasn't been updated for about 10 minutes it says **Open the app to check the status**. Opening the app catches it up. Live Activities follow the app's language, so they're in Greek when the app is.

> **Tip:** Don't see it? Check **iPhone Settings → AnotherSEOGuru → Live Activities** is on. Other paid tools also show a short **Checking** activity while they run, which turns into **Result ready**.

## Reading the results

- **Site health** is the average page score: 100 for a clean page, 90 for notices only, 60 for a warning and 0 for a critical issue, minus points for site-wide problems.
- **Issues by category** groups problems such as status codes, redirects and broken links, titles and descriptions, speed, canonicals and internal links. Each issue explains **Why it matters** and **How to fix**, with the affected URLs.
- **Add to tasks** turns an issue into a task. **Health over time** compares crawls, and **Re-run audit** checks your fixes.
- **Tap a page to inspect it**, or use the related tools: **Page inspector**, **Indexability**, **Page speed** and **Internal links**.

### AI visibility on iPhone

> See where Google's AI Overview cites you, how many visits AI assistants send and how often AI answers mention you.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/ai-visibility

Open **Insights → AI evidence**. It shows four separate kinds of evidence. Each has its own source, dates and limits, so they're never added up into one number.

| Evidence | Source | What it tells you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Searches that showed an AI Overview | Search Console clicks · AI Overview checks | Your clicks and impressions for searches where a check saw an AI Overview, and whether it cited you. |
| Visits from AI assistants | Google Analytics 4 · sessions | Sessions GA4 attributes to ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot, Gemini and similar. |
| Mentions in AI answers | AI answers dataset · per platform | How often AI platforms mention your domain, per platform and check. |
| Live answers to your prompts | Prompt benchmark · answers and citations | Which assistants named or cited you for each tracked prompt, or **Not named**. |

![AI evidence on iPhone showing 582 AI-referred sessions from ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity and Gemini, with a Load AI referrals button](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/iphone/ai-evidence.webp)
![The AI Overview for a search in the SERP explorer on iPhone, marked You're cited, with its source links and People Also Ask below](https://anotherseoguru.com/images/iphone/ai-overview-cited.webp)

## Check whether an AI Overview cites you

1. Open a search in the **SERP explorer** (from its detail screen or from Workspace) and tap **Check**.
2. The summary shows **AI Overview** as **Cited** when your site is among its sources.
3. Scroll to the AI Overview card to read the full text and the sites it links to. **You're cited** appears at the top when one of them is yours.
4. Back in **AI evidence**, searches you've checked are listed with **Cites you** or **Shown, doesn't cite you**.

> **Note:** Search Console doesn't report AI Overview traffic separately. The clicks shown are your normal clicks for searches where a check saw an AI Overview, not clicks from the AI Overview itself.

## Visits from AI assistants

Link a GA4 property to the site (see [Search performance](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/search-performance)), then tap **Load AI referrals**. You get the **AI-referred sessions** for the period and the split by assistant. A fresh report costs 2 credits; cached reports are free for an hour.

> **Warning:** Many AI visits arrive without a referrer and count as direct, so this number is a floor, not the full picture.

## Mentions and prompt checks

**Mentions in AI answers** charts how often each platform mentions your domain. Answers vary between runs, so read the trend rather than a single check. To run new checks, add prompts or compare with competitors, tap **Open AI visibility**. New checks use credits; viewing saved ones is free.

### The AI assistant on iPhone

> Ask questions about your own Search Console data and follow the assistant as it thinks, reads your data and writes.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/assistant

The assistant answers questions about the selected site using your own Search Console data. It writes the finished text (a new title, a rewritten intro, a plan), not just a brief.

## Where to find it

- The **sparkles** button at the top of Today and Insights.
- **Ask the assistant** on a search or page, on a fix, in a task and in the site audit. The question arrives filled in with that context.
- **Ask assistant** on a traffic alert notification, which asks why the site's clicks changed this week.
- Siri: say **Ask AnotherSEOGuru**.

Not sure what to ask? The empty screen has suggestions such as **What should I fix first this week?**, **Why did my clicks change this month?** and **Write better titles for my top pages**.

## What the assistant is doing

While it works, a status card shows each step, so you never stare at a blank screen:

| You see | What's happening |
| --- | --- |
| **Thinking…** | It's reading your question and deciding which data it needs. |
| **Consulting your data…** | It's reading your data. Each source is a line with a spinner that turns into a check, for example **Reading 1,240 searches from the last 28 days**. A source it can't use is marked not available. |
| **Writing…** | The answer appears as it's written. The list of data it read stays visible. |
| Answer ready | The finished answer with a **Sources** chip naming what it used, such as Google Search Console or **Saved AI answer checks**. |

> **Note:** If the connection drops, the answer says it was interrupted. Tap **Try again** to ask the same question again.

## Using an answer

1. **Copy or share it** Use **Copy**, or **Share** to send it to Notes, Mail or a colleague.
2. **Save it as a task** **Save as task** puts the answer on your task list for the site, ready to ship and measure in Work.
3. **Pick up later** The clock button opens **Conversation history**. Search, rename or delete conversations, or start a **New conversation**.

> **Tip:** Be specific: name the page, the search or the period. "Why did /blog/santorini-cost-guide lose clicks in the last 28 days?" gets a better answer than "why is traffic down?".

### Notifications and background refresh

> Choose which push notifications you get, use their buttons and keep the app's numbers fresh in the background.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/notifications-and-background-refresh

The iPhone app receives the same notifications as the web app: new leads and prospect activity, traffic swings, finished reports, task updates and billing notices. You choose which ones.

## Turn notifications on

1. **Open Settings** On Today, tap the grid button at the top left and choose **Settings**, then go to **Notifications**.
2. **Tap Turn on** iOS asks for permission once. If you said no before, the button reads **Open Settings** and takes you to the iPhone's settings for the app.
3. **Pick your topics** Every topic starts on. Switch off the ones you don't want. Your choice applies to this iPhone.

| Topic | When it arrives |
| --- | --- |
| **New leads** | The moment someone asks for an audit, plus prospect activity: a prospect opens or replies to an audit, or views, accepts or declines a proposal. |
| **Traffic ups and downs** | When a site's clicks rise or fall 20% or more in a week, and other alerts. |
| **Reports** | When a scheduled report is ready. |
| **Tasks** | When a task finishes or needs you. |
| **Billing** | Credits running low and payment problems: a failed payment, a trial ending, an upcoming renewal, or a client payment due. |

**Alert settings** sets which alerts you get and how sensitive they are. These settings are shared with the web app.

## Buttons on notifications

Touch and hold a notification to act without opening the app first:

- A new lead has **Call** and **Email**, which dial or write to the person straight away, and **Open**.
- A traffic alert has **Open site**, which opens that site on Today, and **Ask assistant**, which asks why its clicks changed this week.
- Report and task notifications open the right screen when tapped.

## Background refresh

The app refreshes the open site, your site list and the widgets in the background, so the numbers are current when you open it or glance at a widget. iOS decides when that happens based on how you use the app, usually about once an hour at most. Our server can also wake the app with a silent notification for the same refresh.

> **Tip:** If widgets look out of date, check **iPhone Settings → General → Background App Refresh** is on for AnotherSEOGuru, and that Low Power Mode is off. Opening the app always refreshes everything.

> **Note:** Signing out stops this iPhone's notifications and removes the account's Lock Screen activities.

### Widgets and Siri

> Put your clicks, all your sites and this week's fixes on the Home and Lock Screen, and ask Siri how your site is doing.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/widgets

The app comes with three widgets. They show the numbers the app last loaded, so they cost no credits and stay current through [background refresh](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/notifications-and-background-refresh).

| Widget | What it shows | Sizes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Website clicks** | One site's clicks for the last 28 days, with the trend. | Small and medium on the Home Screen; circular, rectangular and inline on the Lock Screen |
| **All sites** | Every site at a glance, with alerts. | Medium and large |
| **Fixes this week** | The fixes worth the most clicks right now. | Small and medium |

## Add a widget

1. **Open the widget gallery** Touch and hold an empty area of the Home Screen until the apps jiggle, then tap **Edit → Add Widget**.
2. **Find AnotherSEOGuru** Search for AnotherSEOGuru, swipe to the widget and size you want, and tap **Add Widget**.
3. **Choose the site** For **Website clicks**, touch and hold the widget, tap **Edit Widget** and pick the site. Add one per site if you like.

For the **Lock Screen**, touch and hold the Lock Screen, tap **Customize → Lock Screen**, then tap the widget area and choose AnotherSEOGuru.

> **Note:** Widget names and descriptions follow your iPhone's language. The widgets themselves show the language you picked in the app.

## Siri and Shortcuts

Three shortcuts work with Siri and in the Shortcuts app without any setup:

| Say | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| "How is my site doing in AnotherSEOGuru?" | Siri reads out the site's clicks for the last 28 days against the 28 before, and the fix worth the most. |
| "Show this week's fixes in AnotherSEOGuru" | Opens the app on this week's fixes. |
| "Ask AnotherSEOGuru" | Opens the [assistant](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/assistant). |

> **Tip:** The Siri phrases are in English for now, even when the app is in Greek.

### iPhone app FAQ

> Quick answers about the iPhone beta, plans and credits, languages, data access and support.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/iphone-faq

**Is the iPhone app on the App Store?**

Not yet. The app is in beta through Apple's TestFlight. Email [support@anotherseoguru.com](mailto:support@anotherseoguru.com?subject=iPhone%20beta%20access) with the subject **iPhone beta access** and we'll send you an invite. See [Get the iPhone beta](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/get-the-beta).

**Do I need a separate subscription for the app?**

No. The app signs in to the same account as the web app and shows your existing plan and credits under **Settings → Plan and credits**. Plans are chosen on the website.

**Does the app use credits?**

Only for the same paid actions as the web app, such as keyword data, the SERP explorer, site audits and fresh Analytics reports. The app shows **Review the credit cost** before anything is charged, and only a completed result is charged. Reading your Search Console data, Today, fixes, tasks and widgets is free.

**Will I see the same fixes as on the web?**

Yes. The app's opportunity engine and its fix, ship and measure loop are ports of the web app's own code, so both rank the same fixes for the same site. Tasks sync both ways.

**Which iPhones are supported?**

iPhone on iOS 17 or later. On iOS 26 and later the app uses Apple's Liquid Glass navigation. It also runs on iPad.

**Is the app available in Greek?**

Yes, the whole app is in English and Greek. Change it in **Settings → Language**. The choice is saved to your account, so our emails and notifications follow it.

**What access does it need to my Google data?**

The same read-only Search Console and Analytics access as the web app. It can read your data; it can't change anything in your Google account.

**Can I try it without connecting a site?**

Yes. Tap **Explore the sample workspace** on the first screen. It uses fictional sites and works offline, so you can try every screen before you connect Google.

**I'm a client of an agency. Can I use the app?**

Yes. Tap **Clients Area** on the first screen and enter the email your agency invited. You'll get a one-time code and see only your reports, shared work and payments.

**Why don't I see the site audit on my Lock Screen?**

Check that Live Activities are on in **iPhone Settings → AnotherSEOGuru**. See [Site audit on iPhone](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/help/iphone-app/site-audit-on-iphone).

**How do I delete my account?**

**Settings → Delete my account**. Type your email to confirm. It deletes the account and its data for good. Cancel a renewing plan in Billing first.

**How do I report a bug in the beta?**

Email support@anotherseoguru.com with a screenshot, what you did and what you expected. Include the version number at the bottom of **Settings**.

### SEO glossary

> SEO, AEO, GEO and Search Console terms in plain words.

Source: https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary

## On-Page SEO

- [On-Page SEO](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/on-page-seo-term): Optimizing elements on a web page to rank for relevant searches.
- [Title Tag](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/title-tag): HTML element specifying a page's title for search results and browser tabs.
- [Meta Description](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/meta-description): HTML attribute providing a brief summary of page content for search results.
- [H1 Tag](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/h1-tag): The main heading tag in HTML, typically used for the primary page title.
- [Heading Structure](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/heading-structure): The hierarchical organization of H1-H6 tags to structure page content.
- [Keyword Density](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/keyword-density): The percentage of times a keyword appears compared to total word count.
- [Image Alt Text](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/image-alt-text): Descriptive text attribute for images that helps search engines and screen readers.
- [Internal Linking](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/internal-linking): Hyperlinks connecting pages within the same website.
- [Content Optimization](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/content-optimization): The process of improving content to rank better and satisfy user intent.

## Technical SEO

- [Technical SEO](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/technical-seo-term): Improving site infrastructure for crawling, indexing, speed, and structured data.
- [Crawling](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/crawling): The process by which search engine bots discover and read web pages.
- [Indexing](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/indexing): The process of storing and organizing crawled pages in search engine databases.
- [Robots.txt](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/robots-txt): A file that instructs search engine crawlers which pages to crawl or avoid.
- [XML Sitemap](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/xml-sitemap): A file listing important URLs to help search engines discover and crawl content.
- [Canonical Tag](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/canonical-tag): HTML element that specifies the preferred version of a page to avoid duplicate content.
- [Structured Data (Schema)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/structured-data): Code markup that helps search engines understand page content and enables rich results.
- [HTTPS](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/https): Secure version of HTTP that encrypts data between browser and server.
- [Hreflang](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/hreflang): HTML attribute that specifies language and regional targeting for international pages.
- [Page Speed](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/page-speed): How fast a web page loads, affecting user experience and search rankings.
- [Mobile-First Indexing](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/mobile-first-indexing): Google's practice of using the mobile version of a site for indexing and ranking.

## Link Building

- [Off-Page SEO](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/off-page-seo): Ranking signals earned outside your website, mainly backlinks and brand mentions.
- [Backlink](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/backlink): A link from one website to another, signaling trust and authority.
- [Anchor Text](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/anchor-text): The visible, clickable text in a hyperlink.
- [Domain Authority (DA)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/domain-authority): A metric predicting a website's ability to rank, based on its backlink profile.
- [Link Equity (Link Juice)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/link-equity): The ranking value passed from one page to another through hyperlinks.
- [Dofollow Link](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/dofollow): A link that passes SEO value and authority to the destination page.
- [Nofollow Link](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/nofollow): A link with an attribute telling search engines not to pass ranking value.
- [Link Building Outreach](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/link-building-outreach): The process of contacting website owners to request backlinks.
- [Toxic Backlinks](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/toxic-backlinks): Low-quality or spammy links that can harm your search rankings.

## Keyword Research

- [SEO (Search Engine Optimization)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/seo): The practice of improving a website so it ranks higher in organic search results.
- [Keywords](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/keywords): Words or phrases users type into search engines to find information.
- [Long-tail Keywords](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/long-tail-keywords): Longer, more specific keyword phrases with lower volume but higher intent.
- [Search Volume](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/search-volume): The number of times a keyword is searched in a given timeframe.
- [Keyword Difficulty](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/keyword-difficulty): A metric estimating how hard it is to rank for a specific keyword.
- [Search Intent](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/search-intent): The underlying goal a user has when typing a search query.
- [Keyword Cannibalization](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/keyword-cannibalization): When multiple pages on your site compete for the same keyword.
- [Keyword Clustering](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/keyword-clustering): Grouping related keywords to target with a single piece of content.
- [Seed Keywords](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/seed-keywords): Starting keywords used to generate broader keyword lists.

## Analytics & Metrics

- [Clicks](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/clicks): The number of times users click on your search result to visit your page.
- [Impressions](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/impressions): The number of times your page appeared in search results.
- [CTR (Click-Through Rate)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/ctr): The percentage of impressions that resulted in clicks.
- [Average Position](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/average-position): The average ranking position of your page for a query in search results.
- [Bounce Rate](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/bounce-rate): The percentage of visitors who leave after viewing only one page.
- [Organic Traffic](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/organic-traffic): Visitors who arrive at your site from unpaid search engine results.
- [Dwell Time](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/dwell-time): How long a user spends on your page before returning to search results.
- [Conversion Rate](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/conversion-rate): The percentage of visitors who complete a desired action.

## SERP Features

- [Featured Snippet](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/featured-snippet): A highlighted answer box that appears at the top of search results.
- [People Also Ask (PAA)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/people-also-ask): An expandable box showing related questions users commonly search.
- [Rich Snippets](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/rich-snippets): Enhanced search results displaying additional information like stars, prices, or images.
- [Knowledge Panel](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/knowledge-panel): An information box appearing on the right side of search results for entities.
- [Local Pack](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/local-pack): A map with 3 local business listings appearing for location-based searches.
- [Image Pack](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/image-pack): A row of images appearing in organic search results.
- [Video Carousel](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/video-carousel): A scrollable row of video results, typically from YouTube.
- [AI Overview (SGE)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/ai-overview): AI-generated summary appearing at the top of search results.

## Local SEO

- [Local SEO](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/local-seo-term): Optimization for map pack and location-based search results.
- [Google Business Profile (GBP)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/google-business-profile): Free Google tool for managing your business's appearance in search and maps.
- [NAP (Name, Address, Phone)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/nap): Business contact information that must be consistent across the web.
- [Local Citations](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/local-citations): Online mentions of your business name, address, and phone number.
- [Local Keywords](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/local-keywords): Search terms that include geographic modifiers or imply local intent.
- [Review Management](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/review-management): The practice of monitoring, responding to, and encouraging customer reviews.
- [Geo-Targeting](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/geo-targeting): Delivering content or results based on a user's geographic location.

## Content Strategy

- [E-E-A-T](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/e-e-a-t): Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness and Trustworthiness: Google's content quality guidelines.
- [Content Decay](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/content-decay): The gradual decline in organic traffic and rankings of older content.
- [Topic Clusters](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/topic-clusters): A content organization strategy linking related articles around a pillar page.
- [Content Gap Analysis](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/content-gap-analysis): Identifying topics competitors cover that you don't.
- [Evergreen Content](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/evergreen-content): Content that remains relevant and valuable long after publication.
- [Thin Content](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/thin-content): Pages with little or no added value for users.
- [Content Freshness](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/content-freshness): How recently content was published or updated.

## Core Web Vitals

- [LCP (Largest Contentful Paint)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/lcp): Measures how quickly the largest content element becomes visible.
- [FID (First Input Delay)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/fid): Measures the time from first user interaction to browser response.
- [CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/cls): Measures visual stability by tracking unexpected layout movements.
- [INP (Interaction to Next Paint)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/inp): Measures overall page responsiveness to user interactions.
- [Page Experience](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/page-experience): Google's combined measure of user experience signals including Core Web Vitals.

## Algorithm & Updates

- [Google Algorithm](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/google-algorithm): The complex system Google uses to rank search results.
- [Algorithm Update](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/algorithm-update): Changes Google makes to its ranking systems.
- [Core Update](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/core-update): Major algorithm updates affecting broad ranking systems.
- [Helpful Content Update](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/helpful-content-update): Update targeting content created primarily for search engines rather than users.
- [Spam Update](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/spam-update): Updates targeting manipulative and spammy SEO tactics.
- [Ranking Volatility](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/ranking-volatility): The degree of fluctuation in search rankings over time.

## AI & SEO

- [AI Mode](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/ai-mode): Google's conversational search surface, which renders answers as interactive cards rather than a list of links.
- [Grounding](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/grounding): Tying a generated answer to a retrievable source, so the claim can be attributed rather than invented.
- [LLM SEO](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/llm-seo): Optimizing content to appear in Large Language Model responses.
- [AI-Generated Content](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/ai-content): Content created by artificial intelligence tools.
- [Zero-Click Search](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/zero-click-search): Searches where users get answers without clicking any results.
- [Semantic Search](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/semantic-search): Search that understands meaning and context, not just keywords.
- [Entity SEO](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/entity-seo): Optimization focused on entities (people, places, things) rather than keywords.
- [AI Autopilot (SEO)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/ai-autopilot): Automated AI-driven SEO optimization and task execution.

## Tools & Platforms

- [Google Search Console (GSC)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/google-search-console): Free Google tool providing search performance data and site health insights.
- [Google Analytics 4 (GA4)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/google-analytics): Google's free web analytics platform for tracking user behavior.
- [SERP (Search Engine Results Page)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/serp): The page displayed by search engines in response to a query.
- [Search Operators](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/search-operators): Special commands to refine and filter search queries.
- [Rank Tracking](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/rank-tracking): Monitoring keyword positions in search results over time.
- [Site Audit](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/site-audit): Comprehensive analysis of a website's technical SEO health.
- [Competitor Analysis](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/competitor-analysis): Researching competitor SEO strategies and performance.
- [SEO Reporting](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/seo-reporting): Regular reports communicating SEO performance and progress.

## Advanced Concepts

- [Crawl Budget](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/crawl-budget): The number of pages Googlebot will crawl on your site in a given time.
- [Index Bloat](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/index-bloat): Having too many low-value pages indexed in search engines.
- [Topical Authority](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/topical-authority): Being recognized as an authoritative source on a specific topic.
- [Pogo-sticking](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/pogo-sticking): When users quickly bounce back to search results and click another result.
- [Redirect (301/302)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/redirect): Sending users and search engines from one URL to another.
- [Log File Analysis](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/log-file-analysis): Analyzing server logs to understand how search engines crawl your site.
- [Site Migration](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/site-migration): Moving a website to a new domain, platform, or structure.
- [YMYL (Your Money Your Life)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/ymyl): Topics that can significantly impact users' health, finances, or safety.
- [Duplicate Content](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/duplicate-content): Substantially similar content appearing at multiple URLs.
- [Noindex Tag](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/noindex): A directive telling search engines not to include a page in their index.
- [Pagination SEO](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/pagination-seo): Handling multi-page content for optimal search engine indexing.
- [Rendering (JavaScript SEO)](https://anotherseoguru.com/en/glossary/rendering): How search engines process and execute JavaScript to see page content.
